title: Teachers at Charter School - 2 positions commencing in 2027
text:
At a glance
Located in Epsom, we are seeking two full-time, permanent teachers, starting in 2027, with a competitive salary aligned with experience, at a knowledge-rich Cambridge Primary school with a strong Catholic ethos.
About the role
We are seeking two exceptional primary school teachers to join Tōtara Point School in full-time, permanent positions starting in 2027.
Tōtara Point is up and running, with an established leadership team, strong culture, and a clear sense of who we are. As a Cambridge International Primary School with a Catholic ethos, you'll join a calm, joyful, and academically ambitious community that uses explicit instruction, high expectations, and strong routines to help every student thrive, especially in literacy and numeracy.
As part of a growing school, you'll help shape classroom practice while working within clearly established systems, with long-term stability and career growth on offer.
Key responsibilities
Teach a knowledge-rich curriculum using explicit instruction and consistent routines
Build strong relationships with students, families, and staff
Deliver Religious Education in line with our Catholic ethos
Uphold the school's Catholic mission through your professional conduct
About you
You're a purposeful, mission-driven teacher who believes all children can achieve with excellent teaching and high expectations. You'll need:
NZ teaching registration or eligibility, and a teaching qualification
Strong classroom practice and behaviour management
Willingness to work in a low-tech school using the Cambridge Primary curriculum
Commitment to discipline, structure, and our Catholic ethos
Experience with the Spalding Method or structured literacy is a significant advantage.
Why join Tōtara Point?
Established culture, strong routines, and a collegial team
Structured Cambridge Primary curriculum
Ongoing training, including Cambridge and Spalding Training
Collaborative planning and engaged families
Tōtara Point Primary School is committed to child safeguarding. Appointment is subject to police vetting and reference checks.

title: Join the Founding Team at Little Taki's Community Kindergarten

visa.text: Please note we are not an accredited employer and are therefore unable to support applications requiring an Accredited Employer Work Visa.

text:
Nightcaps, Southland | Opening January 2027 (Subject to Licensing)
Little Taki's Community Kindergarten is a brand-new, community-focused early childhood service, and we're looking for passionate, qualified teachers to help bring our vision to life. This is a rare opportunity to be part of our founding team, helping shape our culture, learning environments, and the experiences of children and whānau from day one.
We are currently recruiting:
3 qualified early childhood teachers – over two's/preschool room
2 qualified early childhood teachers – under two's room
1 full-time qualified teacher – break cover across the centre
1 part-time qualified teacher – non-contact cover (approximately 15 hours per week)
At Little Taki's, we are creating a warm, homely, rural kindergarten where relationships, play, and belonging are at the heart of everything we do. Guided by Te Whāriki, we value collaboration, innovation, and providing high-quality education and care for every child.
As a service participating in the full pay parity scheme, eligible qualified teachers will be employed in accordance with the current pay parity salary scales, alongside dedicated non-contact time, paid staff meetings, professional growth opportunities, and a supportive team environment.
We know great teachers come with different needs, so we're committed to finding the right people. Flexible working arrangements, including part-time hours and job-share opportunities, will be considered for suitable applicants.
If you hold a recognised early childhood qualification, a current Teaching Council Practising Certificate, and are excited by the opportunity to help establish a new kindergarten, we'd love to hear from you.
Join us in creating something truly special for the children and families of our community.
Little Taki's Community Kindergarten
"Growing confident, curious, and capable learners through connection, play, and belonging."
Please note we are not an accredited employer and are therefore unable to support applications requiring an Accredited Employer Work Visa.

title: Online English Teacher
text:
Aotearoa Infinite Academy is New Zealand's first tuition-free online high school, pioneering accessible, world-class education for students in Years 9 to 13 across all of Aotearoa.
Aotearoa Infinite Academy
We combine international (Pearson Edexcel pre-IGCSE and IGCSE) and national (NCEA Levels 2 and 3) curricula with a flexible, virtual learning model that prioritises wellbeing, belonging, and personalised support.
The opportunity
Teach engaging English through live virtual classrooms to Years 9 to 12 students, delivering Pre-IGCSE, IGCSE, and NCEA Levels 2 to 3 curriculum. Work fully remotely from anywhere in New Zealand while building a supportive, connected learning community.
What you'll do:
Deliver inspiring live online English lessons 5 days per week
Design personalised learning experiences.
build trust-based relationships with students in a virtual environment.
collaborate with a high-calibre team of innovative educators.
support student progress through differentiated instruction.
provide meaningful formative assessment, with quality feedback, feed-forward, and summative assessment, aligned to curriculum goals.
contribute positively to the functioning and growth of the curriculum team.
develop genuine partnerships with, and report to parents and caregivers to support learning.
What we're looking for
Essential:
New Zealand Teaching Registration.
English teaching qualification and subject expertise.
Strong knowledge of NCEA curriculum (Levels 2 to 3).
Excellent communication skills and comfort with digital technology.
Desirable:
IGCSE teaching experience.
Online or blended learning experience.
Familiarity with educational technology and AI platforms.
What we offer:
Opportunity to be part of a pioneering educational initiative in Aotearoa.
Flexible, fully remote working arrangement from anywhere in New Zealand.
Supportive, high-calibre team of educators and leaders.
Chance to make a meaningful difference in the lives of students across the country.
Collaborative, innovative school culture focused on wellbeing and excellence.

title: Qualified Kaiako
institute: Little Blue Penguin Preschool and Nursery Prestons
text:
At Little Blue Penguin, we are a small, relationship-focused centre where tamariki are at the heart of everything we do. We pride ourselves on creating a calm, respectful environment that feels like a home away from home, with a strong emphasis on connection, care, and meaningful learning experiences across our mixed-age setting.
We are looking for a passionate and reliable full time kaiako to join our team. We are a mixed aged centre but this position will be based with our over 2's.
We are also looking for a qualified reliever to join our team on a casual basis.
About the role
While this role is primarily based with our over-twos, we are a mixed-age centre and value teachers who are confident and capable of working across all age groups. We are seeking a passionate, adaptable educator with a strong understanding of Te Whariki and the key guiding documents that underpin quality early childhood practice. You will be committed to building meaningful relationships, creating responsive learning experiences, and contributing positively to a collaborative teaching team.

Ko te whakatauākī e kawe nei i ngā wawata o tō mātou kura, ko:
Oroua Rourou Kai
Rourou ki uta, Rourou ki tai,
Oroua tangata ki te ao-tuuroa
He kura aa iwi mātou, Ko te marau aa Iwi te tūāpapa o tō mātou nei kura. E whai atu tō mātou kura i ngā tikanga me ngā kawa o Waikato, Tainui. He mema anō hoki mātou o Te Rūnanga Nui o ngā Kura ā Iwi o Aotearoa.
E hiahia ana mātou i;
He tangata e mātau ana ki te ao mātauranga me ōna marautanga.

He kaiako e ngākaunui ana ki te whakawhanake i ōna ākonga kia whai wheako ai rātou ki te eke ki roto i te NCEA, ā, e mātau ana ki te Pūtaiao, Ngā Toi, Pangarau.
He ngākau nui ki te tuitui, ki te whakapakari me te whakahāo i ngā tāonga hei koropū mo te iwi ki ngā tau anamata.
E wātea ana te ‘Māori Immersion Teachers Allowance (MITA)’. He tūranga hoki tēnei kia poipoia hei kaiārahi (ka whai utu mō ngā mahi e hāngai ana ki āu haepapa)
Kua tono hoki mātou ki te Teaching Bond Scheme, ā, kua whakaaetia e te MOE tā mātou tono. Ka whakawhiwhia te kaitono ki te $40,000 hei tautoko i tēnei tūnga.
Tukuna mai tō tono me ngā kōrero hāpai pukenga (CV) hei tirotiro mā mātou.

Junior Junction Hamilton is looking for a passionate, caring, and enthusiastic kaiako to join our preschool team, working with children aged 3 to school age.

We are looking for someone who:
Has ECE experience/genuine passion for and thorough understanding of preschool-aged learners.
Is self-reflective and eager to drive their own professional learning.
Recognises themselves as an important resource in the care and education of our children.
Has a genuine passion for exploring bicultural learning and incorporating Te Whāriki into their practice.
Understands assessment processes and can use these to support meaningful learning.
Draws inspiration from children’s interests, strengths, and emerging skills to design engaging learning opportunities.
Brings a fun, positive, and child-focused attitude to each day.

Full-time employment

Full pay parity
A supportive and welcoming teaching team
The opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our preschool learners

title: Resource Teacher Learning and Behaviour Manurewa - 2 positions
text:
An exciting opportunity has arisen to join our collaborative and experienced RTLB team in Manurewa, South Auckland.
Te Huinga Raukura ki Manurewa, RTLB Cluster 12 provides learning and behaviour support across 33 kura and schools within our diverse Manurewa community. We work alongside kaiako, school leaders, whānau and other professionals to strengthen inclusive practice and improve outcomes for ākonga.
We are seeking experienced, reflective and collaborative trained RTLB or teachers who are passionate about supporting the learning, engagement, participation and wellbeing of ākonga.
Successful applicants will:
hold a current full New Zealand practising certificate and have strong teaching experience
build respectful, mana-enhancing relationships with ākonga, whānau, kaiako and school communities
demonstrate culturally responsive practice and commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi
have sound knowledge of inclusive education, neurodiversity and diverse learning and behavioural needs
understand evidence-informed teaching approaches, including the Science of Learning
have up-to-date curriculum knowledge and experience in NZ school settings.
work effectively across individual, group and systems-level contexts to build teacher and school capability
demonstrate strong communication, organisation, collaboration and problem-solving skills.
Experience in leadership, learning support, behaviour, literacy, numeracy or neurodiversity would be an advantage.
Applicants must hold a full New Zealand driver licence and have access to a reliable vehicle.
Applicants without the required RTLB specialist qualification must be eligible and willing to undertake the Postgraduate Diploma in Specialist Teaching (Learning and Behaviour) through Massey University.

title: Online Mathematics Teacher
text:
About Aotearoa Infinite Academy
Aotearoa Infinite Academy is New Zealand's first tuition-free online high school, pioneering accessible, world-class education for students in Years 9-13 across all of Aotearoa. We combine international (Pearson Edexcel pre-IGCSE and IGCSE) and national (NCEA Levels 2 and 3) curricula with a flexible, virtual learning model that prioritises wellbeing, belonging, and personalised support.
The opportunity
Teach engaging mathematics through live virtual classrooms to Years 9-12 students, delivering Pre-IGCSE, IGCSE and NCEA Levels 2-3 curriculum.
Work fully remotely from anywhere in New Zealand while building a supportive, connected learning community.
You'll:
Deliver inspiring live online mathematics lessons five days per week
Design personalised learning experiences
Build trust-based relationships with students in a virtual environment
Collaborate with a high-caliber team of innovative educators
Support student progress through differentiated instruction
Provide meaningful formative assessment, with quality feedback, feed-forward, and summative assessment, aligned to curriculum goals
Contribute positively to the functioning and growth of the curriculum team
Develop genuine partnerships with, and report to parents and caregivers to support learning
What we're looking for
Essential:
NZ Teaching Registration
Mathematics teaching qualification and subject expertise
Strong knowledge of NCEA curriculum (Levels 2-3)
Excellent communication skills and comfort with digital technology
Desirable:
IGCSE teaching experience
Online or blended learning experience
Familiarity with educational technology and AI platforms
We offer:
The opportunity to be part of a pioneering educational initiative in Aotearoa
Flexible, fully remote working arrangement from anywhere in New Zealand
Supportive, high-calibre team of educators and leaders
Chance to make a meaningful difference in the lives of students across the country
Collaborative, innovative school culture focused on wellbeing and excellence
Our commitment
At Aotearoa Infinite Academy, we believe every student deserves access to exceptional learning opportunities, regardless of their circumstances or location.
We are committed to creating an inclusive, supportive environment where all learners can thrive. We welcome applications from candidates who share our vision and values.
How to apply
Please apply via our website in the footer, under the "Join Our Team" link.

title: Deputy Principal / Year 7- 8 Teacher
text:
Upper Moutere School is a vibrant, full primary school. We pride ourselves on our welcoming community culture, strong local curriculum ties, and high standards of learning. We are seeking a forward-thinking, highly organised educator to join our dedicated team.
The role
We are looking for an experienced Year 7-8 classroom teacher to lead our senior students. This is a unique role guiding our students, preparing them for secondary school, and fostering independence, critical thinking, and citizenship.
This position carries the opportunity for Deputy Principal responsibilities (units negotiable based on leadership experience and portfolio area).
Key responsibilities
Senior classroom excellence: Deliver an engaging, differentiated curriculum tailored to Year 7 and 8 learners, with strong competency in structured literacy and core learning areas.
Classroom management and administration: Bring high-level organisational skills to manage classroom routines, assessment tracking, reporting, and student leadership opportunities.
School and community connection: Build positive, collaborative relationships with students, whānau, staff, and the wider rural community.
Leadership experience (DP responsibilities): Assist the Principal in day-to-day school operations, curriculum coordination, PLD support, and pastoral care across the school.
Key requirements
Teaching certification: Full registration with the Teaching Council of Aotearoa New Zealand.
Proven experience: Demonstrated success teaching Year 7 and 8 students, and proven leadership experience.
Exceptional organisation: Outstanding time management, communication skills, and attention to detail in record-keeping and program planning.
Growth mindset: Enthusiasm for continuous professional development, collaborative practice, and ongoing school improvement.
Rural school passion: A genuine desire to embrace and contribute to a close-knit, rural school environment.
What we offer
A welcoming, supportive, and collaborative teaching team.
Dedicated, friendly students and a supportive local whānau community.
A scenic rural working environment in the Tasman region with excellent work-life balance.
Ongoing professional learning and leadership development opportunities.
Management units available for Deputy Principal responsibilities, matched to candidate strengths.
How to apply
To apply, please submit your CV, a cover letter outlining your teaching philosophy and leadership experience, and the contact details for three professional referees.

At Taipa Area School, our vision - “Kia ngātahi te hoe, kia whakatere te waka ki uta” (Navigate together for success) - reflects the strength of our connections with whānau, community, local hāpu and iwi. Grounded in the rich heritage of Ngāti Kahu, we pride ourselves on nurturing genuine relationships with our ākonga, providing a strong sense of belonging, wellbeing, and the foundations for personal and academic success.
We are seeking an outstanding, passionate Leader of Learning, Physical Education & Health, to lead our Physical Education & Health Learning Area and further strengthen teaching, learning, and achievement across Years 7-15. NCEA experience, with knowledge of the newly refreshed NZ Curriculum is a distinct advantage. This position offers an exciting opportunity to shape curriculum delivery, build teacher capability, and champion success for all students. Our kura has a genuine whānau atmosphere, providing the opportunity to build meaningful relationships with students across the school and make a lasting difference in their lives.
Commencing Term 1, 2027 (or by negotiation).
Come join us in Paradise! Doubtless Bay is a beautiful place to live and work. Only 50 minutes drive to Bay of Islands airport, two hours drive to Whangarei and four hours drive to Auckland. Our school is adjacent to Taipa Beach, which we proudly proclaim is the best open-air classroom in Northland.
Our kura is on a waka, putting student engagement and achievement at the forefront of everything we do, supported by hauora and our three core values of Manaakitanga, Painga, and Mahitahi, which we embody in our daily practices.
We welcome applications from NZ-registered teachers looking to contribute to a collaborative, supportive, and forward-thinking team environment.

title: Kaiako / Teacher – Permanent 1 FTTE
text:
Location: Blenheim based with areas that cover Kaikōura / Marlborough
Employment type: Permanent, full-time or a 2x shared part time roles
Commencement: By negotiation
About us
Southern Health School (Te Kura Whaiora ki te Tonga) is a state special school providing education for ākonga in Years 1–13 whose health needs prevent regular school attendance. We work alongside whānau, schools of enrolment, and health professionals to maintain learning and support successful transitions back to school or onward pathways.
About the role
We are seeking an experienced Kaiako / Teacher to join our Blenheim / Kaikōura / Marlborough team.
You will plan, deliver, assess, and evaluate individualised learning programmes aligned with the New Zealand Curriculum / Te Marautanga o Aotearoa. Teaching takes place across community classrooms, homes, health facilities, and other approved locations.
You will work collaboratively with ākonga, whānau, colleagues, schools, and health professionals to support learning, wellbeing, engagement, and positive transition outcomes.
The position is based in Blenheim and requires regular travel throughout Blenheim / Kaikōura / Marlborough. Where a school vehicle is unavailable, you may be required to use a private vehicle, with mileage reimbursed under school policy.
About you
You will have:
Full Teaching Council registration and a current practising certificate
Eligibility to teach in New Zealand
Experience delivering high-quality teaching aligned with the national curricula
The ability to teach or adapt your practice across Years 1–13
A learner-centred, inclusive, and culturally responsive approach
Strong relationship, communication, assessment, and reporting skills
Confidence working independently across flexible settings
Sound digital capability and professional judgement
Commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi
A current full New Zealand driver licence.
Experience supporting ākonga with health, additional learning, behavioural, or complex wellbeing needs is advantageous.
This role is not suitable for beginning teachers.
Employment is covered by the Secondary Teachers’ Collective Agreement. Appointment is subject to satisfactory Police vetting.

title: Kaiako Wharekura
text:
Kei te rapu mātou i ētahi kaiako wharekura, kounga nui, pūkenga rau ki te whakakī i tō mātou tīma. E whitu pea ngā tūranga e wātea ana. Kei te tūwhera mātou ki te whakaranu i ētahi tūranga me he take.
Reo Pākehā ki ngā teina (0.5 FTTE) Tau 9 - Tau 10
Ngā Toi (1.0 FTTE) Wharekura (ka āwhina i ngā kaiako kura tuatahi)
Hākinakina (1.0 FTTE) Wharekura (ka āwhina i ngā kaiako kura tuatahi)
Ngā Kōrero o Mua / Tikanga Tangata (1.0 FTTE) Wharekura whānui
Hangarau (1.0 FTTE) - ahakoa te momo hangarau
Pūoro (1.0 FTTE) Wharekura (ka āwhina i ngā kaiako kura tuatahi)
Pūtaiao (1.0 FTTE) Tau 7 - Tau 10
Tuatahi - me pukenga te tangata, me matatau ki te reo Māori me pēhea hoki te kawe i tana kaupapa i roto i te reo Māori ki nga tamariki, mō ngā tamariki. Nā reira, me ngākau nui tēnei hunga ki nga tamariki, taiohi nei.
Tuarua - he pai mehemea he tohu whakaako tōna heoi, he mea tērā e tāea te whai a tōna nei wā. He pai hoki mehemea e mārama ana ngā tāngata ki te whakatinanatanga o Te Aho Matua me ngā kawenga mō te NCEA.
Kei te hanga kura hou mātou nā reira, piri mai ki te tira hou e whakaritea ana mō te anamata o Ngā Mokopuna. He nui te āwhina kei kōnei, he nui hoki te tautoko me te aheinga kia whai whakangungu mō ngā kaupapa e hia nei.

title: Tumuaki / Principal, U5, Full Primary
text:
Nestled beneath the iconic Taranaki Mounga, where the Mangati flows towards the sea, Bell Block School | Te Kura o Mangati is a proud full primary school within the rohe of Puketapu hapū. With 170 years of heritage, our kura is deeply connected to its community, with fifth-generation families continuing to choose Bell Block School for their tamariki.
We balance our proud history with a modern approach and a commitment to helping every learner succeed. With approximately 480 ākonga and 50 dedicated staff, we are well resourced and offer strong programmes and rich opportunities across academic, sporting, cultural, creative and outdoor pursuits.
Following 10 years of successful leadership, we seek our next Tumuaki | Principal to lead our kura and join our Bell Block School whānau.
Our ideal leader will be someone who
Is visible, relational and approachable — values people, builds genuine relationships and is actively involved in school and community life.
Leads with vision and purpose — brings strong teaching and learning expertise, strategic thinking and fresh ideas, while building on our strengths, traditions and what works well.
Grows people and capability — draws on others’ strengths and expertise, delegates well and creates opportunities for staff to grow.
Builds a positive, inclusive culture — listens deeply, communicates clearly and fosters connection, wellbeing, belonging and shared purpose.
Turns ideas into action — leads purposeful improvement, navigates challenges with calm and resilience, and creates opportunities for every learner to participate, discover and thrive.
Bring your Ability, Attitude and Action to help shape the future of a school with a proud history.
Kaha i ngā wā katoa – Our Best Always.

title: Principal | Tumuaki
text:
Principal | Tumuaki – Taupaki School
Growing for the Future
Country heart. Strong community. Big aspirations. Uniquely Taupaki.
Just beyond the city, Taupaki School offers something increasingly rare – the warmth and connection of a country school, combined with a forward-thinking approach to teaching and learning.
We are a thriving Year 1 to 8 school of approximately 250 students, with a proud history stretching back to 1899. Our people know one another, our staff know their learners, and our community is deeply connected to its school. From Ag Day and our iconic Monster Fireworks to sport, technology, the arts, EOTC and the outdoors, we value the rich breadth of the Kiwi school experience.
At the same time, Taupaki is a school moving confidently forward. Evidence-informed practice, high-impact teaching, structured learning, positive behaviour and wellbeing approaches provide strong foundations for continued improvement.
We are looking for a principal who will:
build strong, trusting relationships and be visible and involved in school life
lead with integrity, kindness, fairness and courage
provide strong educational leadership and hold high expectations for every learner
value and grow our talented staff
strengthen culturally responsive practice and our commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi
lead change thoughtfully – knowing what to protect, what to embed and where to grow
bring the strategic thinking and long-term vision to ensure Taupaki continues to thrive.
If you are a leader who values people, place and possibility, we invite you to come and discover what makes Taupaki uniquely Taupaki.

Collaborate with a high-calibre team of innovative educators.

title: Principal | Tumuaki
text:
Milldale, Auckland roll 327, U5.
Help shape the future of a young, thriving school at the heart of a growing community.
Ahutoetoe School is a rapidly growing Year 0–6 primary school in Milldale, north of Auckland. Established in 2023 and now enjoying purpose-built facilities, our school offers an exciting opportunity for an experienced educational leader to build on strong foundations and guide our next chapter.
Our community values kindness, belonging and the ‘Ahu Way’. We seek an approachable and visible Principal who knows the students, listens to, and acknowledges parents/whānau and leads with integrity, empathy and courage.
Our next principal will:
champion evidence-based teaching, high expectations and measurable progress, with strong foundations in literacy and mathematics
ensure every learner is known, valued, supported and challenged, embracing diversity and additional learning needs
honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi, strengthen cultural responsiveness and embed te reo Māori and tikanga
nurture a collaborative staff culture built on trust, professional growth, wellbeing and shared leadership
communicate openly and build genuine partnerships with whānau, mana whenua and the wider community
combine strategic vision with sound financial, operational and property management as our roll grows
value a broad curriculum, including sport, the arts, inquiry and education outside the classroom.
Our inclusive learning environment includes satellite campuses for Wairau Valley Special School and Northern Health School. You will join dedicated staff, engaged whānau and a supportive Board, with strong resources to advance learning and wellbeing.
We welcome a leader seeking a long-term commitment: someone excited to grow with our school, protect its strengths and develop its identity.
Please refer to the application information for details of school visits and the appointment process.
To arrange a visit to the school please see page 6 of the application pack.

You will:
lead and support a team of kaiako

is an experienced and passionate kaiako with a strong commitment to student success

title: Associate Principal: Leadership and Curriculum. Tagged
Alternative Education Teacher - Literacy and Numeracy
text:
The educator/teacher will work alongside the tumuaki to tailor and deliver individualized education programs to up to 20 young people. They will work alongside youth workers to help develop and implement this programme.

title: Qualified Teacher
text:
We are looking for an experienced, qualified teacher to join our wonderful preschool room at Bear Park Kohimarama. Our centre is a carefully planned, purpose-built learning space, and is loved by children, whanau, and teachers alike.
We are a diverse and enthusiastic team looking for a nurturing and responsive teacher to join us. With our wonderful ratios and endless resources, this is the perfect environment to expand your teaching skillset. We also offer a separate space for teachers to take their breaks and complete their planning/non-contact time away from the centre.
With inspiration from Reggio Emilia, our teachers have a passion for inspiring wonder, creativity, imagination and investigation, fostering children's hundred languages and unravelling their theories alongside them. Bear Park is the premier early learning provider in New Zealand, with over 39 years of industry experience. We are proud to be owned and operated by qualified teachers and offer a wide range of opportunities for our kaiako.
Large learning environments with high-quality resources and generous ratios (1:7).
Dedicated separate space for teachers to relax and enjoy their breaks/planning away from the centre.
Strong individual support from our highly experienced Pedagogical Team * Accessible leaders.
Experienced and supportive teachers.
Ongoing career opportunities.

title: Qualified ECE Kaiako - Full-time, Epsom
text:

build warm, respectful and responsive relationships with tamariki and whānau
plan and provide meaningful learning experiences based on children's interests, strengths and emerging needs
contribute to individual and group planning, assessment and evaluation.
write learning stories and maintain children's portfolios
support an inclusive environment that values children's cultures, languages and identities
work collaboratively with our teaching team and contribute positively to centre life
support our mixed-age group and encourage tuakana–teina relationships between older and younger children
participate in centre experiences such as park walks, gardening, baking, music, science, sensory play and inquiry-based learning
maintain high standards of health, safety and professional practice
engage in ongoing professional learning and reflective practice.

title: Kaiako | Teacher (Part-Time)
text:
Mā te huruhuru ka rere te manu | Adorn the bird with feathers so that it may fly.
Are you a passionate, registered educator looking for a truly rewarding role that transforms lives? Do you believe that every young parent deserves a bright future and a supportive, non-judgmental environment to reach their highest potential?
Hiwa-i-te-rangi Teen Parent Unit
Hiwa-i-te-rangi Teen Parent Unit is on the lookout for an extraordinary Kaiako (0.6 FTE) to join our supportive, award-winning whānau. Named after the star of the Matariki cluster that holds our hopes and aspirations, our unit provides a vibrant, wrap-around secondary education for young māmā, dādā, and parents-to-be aged 24 and under.
We walk alongside our students as they balance the demands of school and raising the next generation. With an on-site childcare center (Kowhai Corner), door-to-door transport, and full-time catering, we remove the barriers so our students can focus on learning.
About the role
In this part-time space, you will create a strengths-based, highly individualised learning environment. Our small class sizes allow you to focus deeply on student goals, mentoring them toward NCEA Levels 1–3, University Entrance, and pathways beyond secondary school.
While we welcome applications from all learning areas, an ability or willingness to teach English, Maths, Social Studies is an advantage.
Who we are looking for
A registered professional: You must hold a current New Zealand Teaching Practising Certificate.
Relationship-driven: You anchor your practice in aroha, manaakitanga, and whanaungatanga. You easily build strong, trust-based connections with youth.
Culturally responsive: You have a sound understanding of tikanga Māori and a commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi in action.
Flexible and innovative: You excel at adapting curriculum delivery to meet unique student situations, celebrating milestones along the way.
Empathetic and empowering: You view young parents through a lens of potential, not statistics, fostering self-belief and independence.

title: Principal U3
text:
Kaipaki School is a year 1 to 8 primary near Cambridge.
Kaipaki school has many positive features. We are a supportive, community minded country school where relationships matter.
We value our rural character, a safe and welcoming environment, strong connections between tamariki and staff, and a collaborative team culture.
Our tamariki are at the heart of our decisions, and our staff bring a rich range of strengths, experience and passions to their work.
We are proud of our sense of togetherness and want to keep growing as a school while holding on to the essence of what makes Kaipaki special.
Our unique location is in a beautiful setting with mature trees and extensive grounds including a large court area, and playground.
The school has a modern administration area and completed recent classroom developments.
Cambridge is located close to Hamilton, has many cultural and leisure activities and has a range of schooling options.
The Board of Trustees is dedicated and supportive of the school and teaching staff.
The roll ranges from 130 to 140 with current projections indicating a stable roll of around 135.
If you are a thoughtful, supportive leader who puts tamariki and staff at the heart of your work, and is committed to serving and strengthening our whole school, we’d love to hear from you.

“Poipoia te kākano kia puāwai” — Nurture the seed and it will blossom.

North Street School is seeking an enthusiastic, future-focused Deputy Principal – Junior School to join our leadership team in our positive, connected, and culturally responsive kura.

Pedagogical Leadership: Deep knowledge of the Junior curriculum, structured literacy, and early learning practices.

title: Montessori Kaiako
text:
Bunny Burrows Montessori | Permanent | 30 - 40 hours per week | Starting early 2027
Bunny Burrows Montessori is looking for a passionate and dedicated teacher to join our preschool team from early 2027.
Our environment is welcoming, nurturing and child-lead. We blend the Montessori philosophy with Te Whāriki, supporting children to become confident, capable and independent learners through hands-on, self-directed learning.
We value sustainability, connection to our community, and caring for our environment, and encourage children to develop an understanding of their role within the wider world.
We are looking for someone who:
Has Montessori training or experience, or a genuine interest in Montessori education.
Understands the importance of the prepared environment and the role it plays in supporting children's independence, concentration and learning.
Enjoys encouraging children's curiosity, independence and confidence.
Builds positive and respectful relationships with children, whānau and colleagues.
Values sustainability and contributing positively to our community.
Montessori experience is preferred, but we are open to meeting the right person for our team. Most importantly, we are looking for someone who is passionate about working with children, has a willingness to learn, and shares our values and approach.
An ECE teaching qualification is not essential.
If you feel you could be a wonderful addition to our team, we would love to hear from you.

title: Agriculture Teacher
text:
The Hauraki Plains has a rich farming history, and ensuring our young people can access this future pathway matters to our school and community.
As we look ahead to 2027, we are seeking an Agriculture Teacher to join our team. Hauraki Plains College is funded for a Trades Academy and currently delivers a range of Agriculture and Horticulture programmes to approximately 300 students. Please note any additional curriculum areas you can teach.
Our college has a collaborative and supportive staff culture and is committed to our vision: Excellence is Our Tradition. Ongoing professional learning and development is a valued part of how we grow and respond to the needs of our students and the evolving education landscape.
Through the Haurakian Charitable Trust, we have access to a 25-acre farm located just 300 metres from the school, where much of our practical teaching takes place. There are long-term plans for the development of this farm, including the possible relocation of an old council depot building to be used as a teaching space.
Hauraki Plains is a great place to live and work, and we enjoy strong connections with our local primary schools and wider community. A school house may be available for rent.
This is a full-time permanent teaching position, beginning 27 January 2027. You are very welcome to come and visit.
To apply, please send your cover letter and CV to Toni Ross at [email: see Gazette] .

Our Board seeks an inspiring, child-centred Principal to lead our close-knit Catholic school. This exceptional opportunity is for an existing school leader ready for the ‘next step’ in their career. The school has a stable roll of 50 students and a principal salary scale equivalent to a U3 school

Faith: Set a welcoming standard where Catholic values are actively lived. Strengthen relationships across the school community and the wider parish.

We are looking for a leader who:
Puts learners first: Has high expectations for every child and is committed to inclusive practice and ensuring all learners experience success and belonging.

text:

In addition to our base school, we have 13 satellite sites and a transition unit. We are seeking an experienced, values-led principal with the specialist knowledge, strategic capability and relational strengths to lead our community confidently into its next stage.
This is an exciting opportunity for a highly experienced senior leader with specialist education experience who understands the complexity of supporting learners with diverse and complex needs across multiple sites.
The successful applicant will demonstrate:
deep knowledge of specialist education, individualised learning, neuro-affirming practice and integrated therapeutic support
successful senior leadership of teaching, learning, people and organisational improvement
the ability to establish a clear educational vision and make sound, timely and evidence-informed decisions
strength in developing staff capability, supporting wellbeing and building effective multidisciplinary teams
clear, open and responsive communication, supported by genuine listening and consistent follow-through
commitment to meaningful partnerships with parents, whānau and the wider community
culturally responsive leadership that honours Te Tiriti o Waitangi and strengthens identity, inclusion and belonging
integrity and transparency, including the courage to address complex matters constructively.

title: Learning Support Coordinator
text:
We are seeking an empathetic, collaborative, and highly capable Learning Support Coordinator (LSC) to join our school. A management unit can be discussed depending on the expertise of the candidate.
As our LSC, you will work closely with our teachers, learning assistants, whānau, and external specialist agencies to ensure that students with additional learning needs receives the targeted support, resources, and inclusive classroom environment they need to thrive. The role will be 0.8 LSC and 0.2 releasing teachers. The way this time is distributed in the week will be discussed.

Student Advocacy & Planning: Identify students with learning support needs, develop and monitor tailored Individual Learning Plans (ILPs), and evaluate progress.
Collaboration & Liaison: Work with classroom teachers, parents/whānau, and external specialists (e.g., Ministry of Education, speech-language therapists, occupational therapists).
Building Capability: Support classroom teachers with inclusive pedagogy, differentiated learning strategies, and effective classroom adaptations.

Transition Support: Support smooth transitions for students moving into our school, between year levels, and transitioning out.

Holds a current New Zealand Practising Certificate.
Has a strong track record of successful teaching and inclusive classroom practices.
Demonstrates exceptional interpersonal and communication skills to build positive, trusting relationships with students, whānau, and staff.
Brings strong organisational skills and experience navigating learning support systems and funding pathways.
Possesses a deep commitment to equity, culturally responsive practice, and upholding Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

Current New Zealand Teacher Registration and Practising Certificate.

Ngā āhuatanga e hiahiatia ana E haurapa ana mātou i tētahi Tumuaki:
E pūmau ana ki te reo Māori, ngā tikanga, me Te Aho Matua.
He kaiārahi titiro whakamua, e whai ana i te hiranga mātauranga
He tohunga whakawhanaunga, e mahi tahi ana me te whānau, ngā pouako, me ngā kaimahi
He mātanga ki te marautanga me ngā whakahaerenga kura

Massey High School is seeking a qualified teacher of Health and Physical Education to join our dynamic Health/PE Faculty for a one year fixed term position commencing at the start of Term 1 in 2027. The successful candidate will be a NZ registered teacher with NCEA experience able to support a knowledge-rich curriculum and work collaboratively in a team environment. Ability to teach Health to all levels will be an advantage. Ongoing engagement in professional development will be integral to this position, along with a willingness to participate in extra-curricular or co-curricular activity as part of the wider life of the school. Some interviews may commence prior to the closing date of this advertisement.
Closing date Tuesday 27th October 2026

title: Senior Teacher (Year 6-8)

visa.text: Be eligible to work in Aotearoa New Zealand.

text:
Our senior learners are curious, enthusiastic, and ready for new challenges—and they’re looking forward to meeting their new teacher. Could it be you?
We are seeking a passionate senior teacher to inspire our Years 6–8 ākonga, build on their learning foundations, and prepare them for the next stage of their journey. You’ll bring strong classroom practice, a commitment to collaboration, and a passion for learner leadership and continuous improvement.
Why Kuratau School?
Imagine teaching with the lake and mountains as your backdrop! Just 20 minutes from Tūrangi and an hour from Taupō, our small rural kura offers a stunning natural setting and a strong sense of community.
Relationships are at the heart of everything we do. We value teamwork, professional growth, and equitable outcomes for all ākonga. Join a supportive team committed to engaging learning experiences and helping every learner thrive.
About you
You will:
Have experience teaching Years 6–8 within the New Zealand Curriculum.
Hold a current Teaching Council practising certificate (full registration preferred).
Be eligible to work in Aotearoa New Zealand.
Build positive relationships with ākonga, whānau, colleagues, and the wider community.
Demonstrate strong curriculum knowledge and effective teaching in literacy and mathematics, including Structured Literacy.
Use assessment to respond to learning needs and accelerate progress.
Contribute to collaborative planning, professional learning, and school-wide improvement.
Uphold Te Tiriti o Waitangi and value the identities, languages, and cultures of all learners.
Foster independence, resilience, and leadership through high expectations, engaging learning, and a sense of humour.
Ready to make a difference in a connected rural kura? We’d love to hear from you!
Help our ākonga Learn, Grow, and Lead at Kuratau School.
This position qualifies for the Teacher Bonding Scheme (TBS).
This position will commence at the start of Term 1 2027.

title: Classroom Teacher
text:
Learning that creates opportunity – Na te matauranga ngā ahei i hanga
An exciting opportunity exists for an inspiring classroom teacher at Appleby School from 28 January 2027. The role is likely to be in Years 4–8.
We are seeking a teacher who is committed to providing the very best learning opportunities for our tamariki, demonstrating māia (bravery) in their pedagogy, manaaki (care) for our community, and a deep commitment to ako (learning).
The successful applicant will:
Build positive, learning-focused relationships with all ākonga and whānau.
Support our PP4L (Positive Practice for Learning) approach to create a calm, safe and engaging classroom.
Deliver high-quality, inclusive teaching of the refreshed curricula, using assessment information to accelerate progress, particularly in writing.
Display a strong commitment to uplifting te reo me ōna tikanga Māori.
Work collaboratively as part of a supportive, reflective team.
Applicants must hold full Teaching Council registration and a current practising certificate.
Position commences: 28 January 2027
Please visit our website to find out more about our kura.
Contact [email: see Gazette] for an application pack.
The successful applicants will be safety checked in line with the Children's Act 2014.

title: Kaiako/Teacher K1 (1.0) - Comrie Park Kindergarten

visa.text: Applicants must reside and be eligible to work in New Zealand at the time of applying.

text:
The Northland Kindergarten Association (NKA) is seeking an experienced, passionate and collaborative teacher who values strong relationships with children, whānau, and the wider community to join the dedicated team at Comrie Park Kindergarten in Matarau, Whangārei. This position will commence on the 6th of January 2027.
Comrie Park Kindergarten operates five 6-hour sessions each week for 40 children aged two to six years. As part of NKA's network of 25 kindergartens, you will be supported by experienced professional practice leaders and a dedicated management team, with ongoing opportunities to strengthen your teaching practice, engage in professional learning and support for wellness.
Comrie Park Kindergarten have a strong commitment to sustainable partnerships with community and has an established Ngāhere Programme. Manaakitanga and Kaitiakitanga underpin the team’s practice and culture. This role is ideal for a teacher who enjoys working closely with whānau and inspiring active, curious children through exploration and outdoor learning.
If you are an inspiring educator who is passionate about empowering young learners, positive, driven, values professional growth and wants to make a meaningful difference in the lives of tamariki and their whānau, we would love to hear from you.
Applicants must hold a recognised New Zealand ECE qualification (minimum Dip Teaching ECE), current practicing certificate, and first aid certificate. Applicants must reside and be eligible to work in New Zealand at the time of applying.
Closing date for applications: 2.00 pm Monday 9 November 2026.
Northland Kindergarten Association adheres to the employment conditions as offered in the Kindergarten Teacher, Head Teachers and Senior Teachers Collective Agreement 2026-2028
Download an application pack and a position description from the NKA website www.nka.org.nz or email [email: see Gazette] to request an application pack and position description.
Email Applications to: [email: see Gazette] or post to: Appointments Secretary, Northland Kindergarten Association, PO Box 4005, Whangarei, 0141

title: Classroom Teacher (Year 3-5)
text:
Tagged position. Join a wonderful, caring, and supportive school community where our values come to life in a warm, positive environment every day!
We seek an enthusiastic, passionate, well-organised, highly skilled teacher, capable of teaching multi-level classes (Years 3 to 5). The successful applicant will be required to have sound knowledge and strengths in Literacy and Mathematics and will highly value strong collegiality with school colleagues.
We are looking for teachers who:
Are great team players with a sense of humour and strong relational skills
Spark curiosity and foster the joy of learning
Embrace inclusion, value diverse learning needs, and demonstrate cultural competence
Possess great NZ Curriculum knowledge, experience with Structured Literacy and fluency with Digital technology.
Hold a New Zealand teacher registration (or be eligible to obtain it).
If you are passionate about making a difference, raising student achievement, and considering yourself a lifelong learner, our vibrant, progressive environment with fantastic students and a supportive community would be the ideal position for you.
A willingness and ability to take part in religious instruction appropriate to the Seventh-day Adventist special character of the school and demonstrate the capabilities to maintain curriculum programmes and activities that reflect the school’s special character, which are conditions of this appointment. Note that the special character of the School is defined as the faith system made up of the Christian beliefs, values and lifestyle of the Seventh-day Adventist Church.

Please email your CV and covering letter with 3 nominated references to the School Principal to request a job application. Please state other teaching strengths and experiences; email [email: see Gazette]

title: Deputy Principal/SENCo
text:
Are you passionate about supporting diverse learners? Do you have experience navigating learning support systems and ensuring every child reaches their full potential? Are you an energetic, enthusiastic and motivated educator willing to join our senior leadership team?
The start date is 28 January, 2027.
We are looking for someone who:
hold current New Zealand Teacher Registration
understands Tier 2 and Tier 3 students with high and complex needs
is confident in navigating Ministry and external support processes (ORS, IWS, HHNF, RTLB, IRF, LLI, ESOL)
brings experience in SENCO and/or LSC roles or similar
enjoys collaborating and working as part of a team
is a solutions-focused, creative thinker
is highly organised and demonstrates high levels of professionalism.
The successful applicant will:
work with the Deputy Principal around referrals for special needs intervention, both learning and behavioural, and determine the appropriate level of support needed
lead the learning support team, providing PLD, support and feedback
lead and facilitate Learning Assistant and staff professional training and support, while collaborating with the Deputy Principal and Principal to design and implement IEPs, ILPs, and Individual Behaviour Plans
attend transition meetings and co-construct transition plans
maintain clear and consistent communication with whaanau, caregivers, and external agencies to ensure cohesive support for students
coordinate and/or assist with the preparation, delivery and evaluation of programmes to meet the needs of staff, students and whaanau
complete referrals, induction meetings, observations and follow ups as required/appropriate
provide coaching for teachers in regard to inclusive practices.
Additional roles and responsibilities:
Working with the Leadership team to organise and manage the day-to-day running of the school
Ensure teaching and learning is implemented and delivered well across the kura
Manage and organise professional development and learning opportunities for staff

title: Teacher of Food Technology and Hospitality
text:
Queen Charlotte College is a co-ed secondary school (Yr7 - 13) located in the beautiful town of Picton, gateway to the South Island. Picton is nestled in the stunning Marlborough Sounds, a short flight from Wellington and easy driving to Christchurch and Nelson.
We are known for our supportive, inclusive whānau environment, where strong relationships and student wellbeing are at the heart of everything we do. Our staff work collaboratively to ensure every learner feels valued, supported, and inspired to succeed.
We are seeking an enthusiastic and passionate Food Technology and Hospitality teacher to join our team in a permanent full time position.
We are looking for a suitably qualified teacher with relevant hospitality industry qualifications and practical industry experience, including the expertise required to support the delivery and assessment of Level 2 and Level 3 Hospitality standards and meet Consent to Assess requirements.
Our specialist hospitality classroom is brand new, having opened in January 2025, and provides an excellent environment for practical, hands-on learning. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who can bring industry knowledge into the classroom, inspire students and help them develop the practical skills and confidence needed for future pathways in the food and hospitality industry.
The successful applicant will be passionate about engaging students, building positive relationships and delivering high-quality learning experiences.
This is a permanent full time position commencing 27 January 2027, or earlier by mutual agreement.
School housing is available.
Assistance with moving costs may be available to the successful applicant.

title: Teacher of Mathematics
text:
Opportunity to teach Year 13 mathematics with statistics along with Level 1 and Level 2 classes.
Lindisfarne College is a state integrated Year 7–13 day and boarding school for boys in Hawke’s Bay. We have a proud record of outstanding academic and co-curricular achievement that forms an important part of our special character. Our college site, located on the outskirts of Hastings, offers expansive playing fields and top-class facilities for our young men to develop their sporting and cultural passions.
We are seeking an exceptional full-time teacher with the ability and willingness to teach junior and senior mathematics.
As a special character school, you will be required to support the Christian values that underpin our approach and contribute to the extra-curricular programme at the college.
The working environment at Lindisfarne College encourages innovative teaching of boys and seeks to meet the individual learning needs of each student. The successful candidate would join a well-resourced, supportive, collaborative and enthusiastic mathematics department.
Lindisfarne College is a well-resourced school offering small class sizes and highly motivate, self-disciplined students. Staff benefit from daily cooked lunches, generous leave provisions and a positive, supportive environment. A competitive remuneration package is available, including the teacher salary scale and an additional RRR allowance.
The terms and conditions, including base salary, for this position is set by the Secondary Teachers Collective Agreement 2025 – 2027. Individuals’ actual base salary will be established by a salary assessment once a role is confirmed.
The position is full-time and will commence in Term 1, 2027.

text:

text:

title: LSC - Learning Support Coordinator (new position)
text:
Stoke School is looking for an experienced, inclusive and collaborative educator to join our team as our Learning Support Coordinator (LSC). The successful applicant will be well supported and work closely with the Principal and DPs to ensure the best possible support and outcomes for our learners.
This position has arisen from the rollout of Learning Support Coordinators across the country and is available from the start 2027 (0.37 FTTE funded - staffing as a 0.4 FFTE).
This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and strengthen learning support across our full primary school. We are looking for someone who understands that effective learning support begins with knowing our ākonga, recognising their strengths and needs, and working alongside teachers, whānau and specialists.
We are a community of kind, curious, creative, confident and active learners who reach for great heights, helping to shape the way we work in our learning community and guiding our programmes as we work together towards implementing this vision. Stoke School is a wonderful and rewarding learning community, where people are warm and welcoming.
You will:
help ensure ākonga with diverse and additional learning needs receive timely, practical and well-coordinated support
contribute to our inclusive culture
support early identification of learning needs and interventions
coordinate individual learning support plans
work with teachers and teacher aides to strengthen classroom practice
use a range of strategies and assessments to inform learner strengths and needs
support parents and whānau to understand processes and guide decision making
liaise with specialist services, including RTLB and the Ministry of Education
support transitions,maintain accurate, confidential records with adherence to privacy requirements
We are looking for someone who:
holds a current New Zealand teacher registration and certification
has experience supporting neurodivergent ākonga and those with diverse learning needs
understands inclusive education, assessment, evidence-informed interventions and Universal Design for Learning. Is a relationship based learning practioner with good coaching skills.

title: ECE Qualified Teacher

visa.text: Applicants for this position must have NZ residency or a valid NZ work visa

text:
Our beautiful childcare centre has been family-owned and operated for over 30 years, and is a well-established and respected service in Mt Eden. Amidst a quiet residential street our carefully repurposed houses cater specifically for the birth to five age group and have been designed to allow for space, flexibility of routines and plenty of ‘elbow-room’ for all children to engage and explore.
Our vision is to create a relaxed home-away-from home for young children where their day is unhurried and nurturing relationships form the basis of learning and growth.
We currently seek a new team member to partner with us in the provision of high-quality early learning experiences:
We welcome applications from candidates who are qualified ECE teachers and demonstrate essential skills including professional knowledge about the learning and development of children (0-5 years old), an ability to meaningfully document children’s learning and an understanding of Te Whāriki and its implementation.
You will be a flexible team player, have strong communication skills, be able to use your initiative and are committed to your professional learning.
It is preferable that applicants will have an understanding or familiarity with the Montessori Method. This pedagogy provides a framework from which our programme takes its inspiration. Experience is not essential though you need to be willing to embrace this approach.
Suitable applicants will demonstrate an understanding of best practice, be a flexible team player and willing to support our Christian philosophy.
Applicants for this position must have NZ residency or a valid NZ work visa
To find out more see our website.

title: Year 7-8 Classroom Teacher
text:
We are looking for a classroom teacher to join us in 2027. We are looking for someone who is excited to help our students reach their full potential. If that sounds like you, we’d love to have you join our team!
At our intermediate school, collaboration and growth are at the heart of what we do. Teachers get over 30 hours of release time each term, and syndicate teams meet together to plan, collaborate, and focus on professional development – which cuts down on after-school hui!
Your role will include crafting engaging lessons for Year 7 and 8 students that bring the whole curriculum to life. You’ll integrate Te Ao Māori and sustainability to create meaningful learning experiences, foster a positive classroom where critical thinking, problem-solving, and teamwork flourish, and build strong connections with students, parents, and whānau. You’ll also help shape and improve our strongly localised curriculum.
We’re looking for someone with a New Zealand teaching qualification and experience or a genuine interest in working with intermediate-aged students.
In return, you’ll find a supportive and collaborative workplace where your contributions make a real difference. We offer meaningful professional development tailored to your growth, along with a well-resourced school environment that supports your creativity.
We want someone energetic and enthusiastic who thrives in a dynamic setting and is ready to engage fully in school life. Building strong, positive relationships with young adolescents is crucial. If you enjoy integrated, localised learning and value being part of a team, you’ll fit right in.
This position qualifies for the Teacher Bonding Scheme (TBS). The eligible teacher recruited for this vacancy will receive annual payments that accumulate to a maximum of $40,000 (before tax) after 5 years. See Teacher Bonding Scheme for more information.
When applying, please highlight your key strengths in your cover letter—we want to know what sets you apart.

title: Classroom Teacher
text:
Kauri Park School is a small, close-knit school surrounded by beautiful native bush on Auckland’s North Shore. We have wonderful tamariki, a supportive community and a team of teachers who care deeply about providing the best possible learning experiences for every child.
Due to a teacher taking parental leave, we are looking for an excellent teacher to join our team in a fixed-term position.
The successful applicant will be a reflective and capable classroom teacher with strong knowledge of teaching literacy and mathematics. You will have high expectations for learners, work collaboratively with colleagues, and be committed to creating a classroom where children feel known, supported and challenged to do their best.
We are looking for someone who is willing to grow professionally, contribute positively to our school community, and bring energy and enthusiasm to their teaching. A commitment to continuing to grow your capability in te reo Māori and Te Ao Māori is important to us.
Our vision is to grow good people who make their community better, and our values of Atawhai, Manawanui and Ū Kaha are central to how we work and learn together.
If you are a passionate teacher who wants to be part of a supportive team and make a genuine difference for our tamariki, we would love to hear from you.

title: Classroom Teacher (Year 3-6)
text:
Kauri Park School is a small, close-knit school surrounded by beautiful native bush on Auckland’s North Shore. We have wonderful tamariki, a supportive community and a team of teachers who care deeply about providing the best possible learning experiences for every child.
We are looking for an excellent permanent full-time teacher to join our team. The successful applicant could teach anywhere across Years 3–6, with the specific year level negotiated later.
We are looking for someone who is highly relational and exceptional at building strong, positive relationships with children. You will know your learners well, create a classroom where they feel safe, valued and challenged, and bring warmth, consistency and high expectations to your teaching.
Strong classroom practice matters to us. We also value teachers who are reflective, collaborative and willing to keep growing professionally. A genuine commitment to te reo Māori, Te Ao Māori and culturally responsive practice is important to us.

title: Assistant to the HOD Mathematics (2MU and 1MMA)
Kaiako Rūmaki – Ngā Tau 0–8
text:
E rapu ana mātou i tētahi kaiako ngākau nui, pukumahi hoki hei whakaako i ā tātou tamariki i roto i te whānau Purapura, Ngā Tau 0–2, Heoi, e pai ana te korero mena he kaiako mō tētahi atu taumata ako.
Ko te tino kaitono he tangata e matatau ana ki te reo Māori me ōna tikanga, e ū ana ki te kounga o te whakaako, ā, e hiahia ana hoki ki te mahi ngātahi ki roto i tētahi tīma kaiako kaha, tautoko hoki.
He kura motuhake a Te Kura ō Te Pāroa e ū ana ki te reo Māori, ki te mātauranga o Ngāti Awa me ngā tikanga o te kura. E whanake tonu ana mātou i tā mātou whakamahinga o Aka Mātauranga (High Impact Teaching Practices), kia mārama, kia whai tikanga, kia whai hua hoki te whakaako mā roto tonu i te reo Māori.
Ka tautokohia ngā kaiako ki te whakawhanake tonu i ā rātou mahi whakaako, tae atu ki te whakaako mārama, ngā tikanga whakauru i ngā ākonga katoa, te arotake auau, ngā mahinga akomanga tōtika me ngā rautaki e hāngai ana ki te āhua o te ako me te maumahara o te tamaiti.
Mēnā e ngākau nui ana koe ki te reo Māori, ki ngā tamariki, ki te ako tonu hoki hei kaiako, nau mai, tukuna mai tō tono.
He pai pea, tēnei tūranga mō tētahi kaiako tīmata.

title: ECE Kaiako - Over 2's
text:

title: Teacher - Permanent 0.6 to 1FTTE - Various Locations
allowances: Regional Health School Unit and Special Duties Allowance
text:
Opportunities for permanent teachers in these locations: Hawke’s Bay, Horowhenua, Hutt Valley, Kāpiti, Manawatū, Porirua, Wairarapa, Wellington, Whanganui. We are also looking for casual and long term relievers.
About us
Central Regional Health School is a state special school providing education for ākonga in Years 1–14 whose health needs prevent regular school attendance. In partnership with whānau, schools of enrolment and health professionals, we support students to maintain their educational programmes and successfully transition back to their school of enrolment or onwards.
The role
We are seeking adaptable, empathetic, motivated and experienced kaiako / teachers for rewarding permanent roles (0.6FTTE to fulltime) across central North Island
Deliver teaching in students’ homes, local schools, health settings and other community venues
Work one-on-one and/or with small multi-level groups
Adapt the New Zealand Curriculum (Levels 1–8) to meet individual learning and health needs
Plan, deliver, assess and evaluate individual learning programmes
Collaborate closely with schools of enrolment, whānau and health professionals
Travel daily is required
Potential to work across multiple CRHS sites
About you
The ideal applicant will be:
Flexible, patient, innovative and self-motivated
An experienced NZ registered teacher with a current practising certificate
Knowledgeable across the NZ Curriculum (Levels 1–8), with at least five years’ successful teaching experience
The ability to teach or adapt your practice across Years 1–13
A learner-centred, inclusive, and culturally responsive approach
Strong relationship, communication, assessment, and reporting skills
Confidence working independently across flexible settings
Sound digital capability and professional judgement
Commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi
Skilled at working collaboratively within multi-disciplinary teams
Requirements
Current full, clean NZ driver licence
Access to a private vehicle for work travel where a school vehicle is unavailable.
Please make it clear which region(s) you are available to work. These roles are not suitable for beginning teachers.

title: Assistant Rector - Teaching and Learning
text:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced and inspiring educational leader to join the Senior Leadership Team at Waitaki Boys’ High School as Assistant Rector – Teaching and Learning.
This is a key professional leadership role, with a strong focus on leading and strengthening teaching and learning across the school. The successful applicant will be a respected colleague, mentor and leader who builds positive relationships with staff and students alike.
Working collaboratively with teachers, support staff and fellow senior leaders, the Assistant Rector will help foster a positive, supportive and effective learning environment where staff feel valued and supported to grow professionally, and students feel encouraged to seek advice, guidance and support.
The successful applicant will:
demonstrate strong leadership
have sound professional judgement
show a commitment to continuous improvement
work well alongside colleagues to enhance teaching practice
promote student achievement
support the ongoing development of the school.
About Waitaki Boys' High School
With a roll of over 440 students, Waitaki Boys’ is “enriched by a proud heritage, but forward-looking and progressive in our task of educating boys to meet the challenges of the new millennium.”
Our inclusive school culture encourages students to participate, contribute and achieve across a wide range of academic, leadership, sporting, arts and cultural opportunities, both inside and outside the classroom.
Our vision is to develop “inspiring young men of outstanding character.”
Why Oamaru?
Oamaru offers a unique lifestyle on the beautiful Otago coast. Recognised by Lonely Planet among its Top 50 Destinations Around the World for 2027, the town is renowned for its striking Victorian limestone architecture, thriving Steampunk culture and colonies of little blue penguins.
With its blend of history, creativity and coastal charm, Oamaru is a wonderful safe place to live and work.

title: Teacher
text:
Are you the kind of teacher who makes a lasting difference in the lives of children?
Invercargill Middle School is looking for an exceptional, passionate and dedicated teacher to join our amazing team!
We are a small, vibrant and wonderfully diverse inner-city school where relationships matter, every child is known and valued, and our staff genuinely care about making a difference.
We are looking for someone who brings energy, enthusiasm, warmth and high expectations to their teaching. Someone who doesn't just teach the curriculum but inspires, challenges and empowers every learner to succeed.
Our ideal teacher will:
Have strong curriculum knowledge and proven expertise in Structured Literacy and mathematics, delivering explicit, effective and engaging teaching.
Build genuine, positive relationships with tamariki, whānau and colleagues.
Create a calm, inclusive and well-structured classroom where every child feels safe, valued and ready to learn.
Hold high expectations and believe wholeheartedly that every child can achieve success.
Be reflective, adaptable and committed to continually growing their practice.
Understand that relationships are the foundation of learning and that behaviour is communication.
Be a collaborative team player who brings positivity, initiative and a willingness to go the extra mile.
At IMS, our vision E Tū Atu Nei – Stand up, stand strong, and be proud guides everything we do.

title: Year 7 and 8 Pedagogical Leader
text:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an inspiring and experienced educational leader to join Hingaia Peninsula School as our Year 7 and 8 Pedagogical Leader from Term 1, 2027. The role comes with 2 MU and 0.1 leadership release. The Sports Coordinator role is also available with 0.1 release and 1MU.
We are proud of our vibrant, multicultural community, our amazing students and strive to live our vision: Inspired Learners Collaboratively Creating Sustainable Futures. We are looking for a leader who is passionate about pedagogy, student agency and teacher growth, and who thrives in a dynamic environment where flexibility, resilience, commitment, initiative and a good sense of humour matter.
You will:
lead and support our Year 7 and 8 team of six teachers inclusive of the technology programme; building a positive, dynamic team
model strong culturally responsive teaching and learning practice, including curriculum implementation, assessment, UDL and evidence-informed practice
design engaging, localised learning experiences that empower students and promote agency
provide strong academic and pastoral leadership, with student wellbeing and success at the centre
build respectful partnerships with students, staff, whānau and our HPS community
work collaboratively with senior leadership to progress school priorities and model our values of Manaakitanga, Whānaungatanga and Kaitiakitanga.
We value leaders who lead by example, communicate clearly, navigate complexity with empathy, and put people - especially our students, first.
Come and join a collaborative, future-focused kura that values relationships, kids being kids and going the extra mile for our students.

title: Scale A Teacher
text:
We seek a scale A teacher to lead a mixed level class in the senior primary school.
What makes our school different for teachers?
To provide balance and opportunities to practise self care, we offer approximately 2 blocks of release as a syndicate every week. This enables us to reduce after school meetings and open up more opportunities for collaboration, induction and ongoing support.
In 2027, we will also provide a teacher aide in every class to support the co constructed curriculum changes and accelerate learning in Literacy and Maths.
We respect teacher professionalism and expertise. We are really proud of how we have developed our English and Maths Curriculum Frameworks to reduce teacher workload, while best supporting learners. We will embed our English and Maths curriculum framework, whilst beginning the co-constructed implementation of the science and Social Science Curriculum in 2027 based on our understanding of the neuroscience behind how the brain learns. At the same time come with the desire to question and be questioned to drive culturally responsive, collaborative improvement.
The Attitude of Gratitude (A conscious decision to give and receive a deeper expression of appreciation and acknowledgement of others. It is a positive emotion which is self replicating, elicits joyfulness, builds social relationships and has a positive effect on the well being of all).
Visiting our school is strongly recommended and making time to have a hot drink and a chat with the principal Jason Ataera or Deputy Principal Olive Masina would be warmly received.
Applications close at 3pm, Friday 30 October.
Interviews completed and the successful candidate notified by Friday 6 November.

title: Small Group Intervention Teacher - Literacy and Maths
text:
Otaua School seeks an enthusiastic, skilled, and highly motivated teacher to join our team in a full-time, fixed-term intervention position in 2027.
This is an exciting opportunity for a passionate educator who believes every child can make progress and enjoys working with students in small groups to accelerate learning, build confidence, and experience success.
The successful applicant will work across the school, providing targeted teaching and support, with a particular focus on Literacy and Mathematics.
We are looking for someone who:
Has strong curriculum knowledge and effective teaching practice, particularly in literacy and mathematics
Is BSLA (Better Start Literacy Approach) trained, with the knowledge and confidence to effectively implement targeted literacy interventions.

Works collaboratively with classroom teachers and school leaders to ensure interventions complement classroom learning.
Is reflective, adaptable and committed to making a measurable difference to student achievement.
At Otaua School, we are committed to creating a positive, inclusive and learning-focused environment where students and staff are supported to thrive.
If you are passionate about accelerating progress and making a genuine difference to student learning, we would love to hear from you.

title: Special Education Needs Coordinator SENCO
allowances: 2 Management Units and 2 Middle Management Allowances
text:
Ao Tawhiti Unlimited Discovery is a designated character state school based in Ōtautahi Christchurch’s central business district. We have a fundamental tenet that the child is central in directing their own learning so that enthusiasm and love of learning is retained. Our students value the choice, flexibility and respect that our style of education provides them.
Our core values are whanaungatanga, kaha, aroha, whakaute and tiakitanga. These values are present in everything we do.
Sadly, our SENCO is retiring and we are looking for an exceptional SENCO to replace her. The successful candidate will be a fully registered teacher who is flexible and innovative in their practice. They will have a strong understanding of Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and how to embed culturally sustaining practice to support success for all our students. They will also have a strong understanding of how to support inclusive education practices, navigate the external resources available through the Ministry of Education and other support networks. The successful candidate will be the line manager for teaching assistants, so experience leading staff, supporting Special Assessment Conditions and managing resources would be helpful.
We ask that interested candidates come into Ao Tawhiti for a tour before submitting an application as we are different to the majority of schools in Aotearoa.

title: Teacher of Technology – DVC and/or Product Design
text:
Ormiston Senior College is a Year 11–13 coeducational public school in East Auckland. We are a future-focused school with a strong commitment to student agency, personalised learning and innovative, student-centred teaching.
We are seeking an enthusiastic Technology teacher to join our collaborative and creative team. There is flexibility within the position to teach Design and Visual Communication (DVC), Product Design, or a combination of both, depending on the strengths and experience of the successful applicant.
For us, personalised learning means high-quality, culturally inclusive teaching that is responsive to the different ways our students achieve their best. He waka eke noa.
Product Design at Ormiston Senior College follows the design process, giving students opportunities to explore, develop and refine ideas through modelling and making. Experience with CAD, CAM and 3D printing would be beneficial.
In DVC, students develop and communicate their design ideas through physical drawing and digital design tools. Experience with a range of drawing techniques and digital design software would be beneficial.
The successful applicant will demonstrate a commitment to:
collaborative teaching and learning within and across curriculum areas
building strong connections with ākonga and whānau
supporting student agency and creative, innovative approaches to learning
developing an understanding of mātauranga Māori and honouring our obligations under Te Tiriti o Waitangi.
We welcome applications from teachers who are passionate about Technology education, enjoy working collaboratively and want to provide engaging, authentic learning experiences for our students.
As with all teaching positions at Ormiston Senior College, the successful applicant will also be a Learning Advisor, supporting and guiding a group of students in their pathways, wellbeing and academic success.
Please send a cover letter, completed general appointment form along with your CV.
