title: Guidance Counsellor (0.6 FTTE)
text:
Are you passionate about supporting the wellbeing, resilience and success of young people?
We are seeking an experienced and compassionate Guidance Counsellor (0.6 FTTE) to join our dedicated student support team. This is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our students while working in a supportive, inclusive and student-centred environment.
Located in the picturesque coastal community of Riverton, Aparima College is a Year 7-13 co-educational secondary school committed to empowering learners to achieve personal excellence through strong relationships, high-quality learning, and a culture of belonging.
The role
The Guidance Counsellor will:
Provide confidential individual counselling and support to students.
Work proactively with students, whānau, staff and external agencies to promote student wellbeing and engagement.
Support students experiencing social, emotional, behavioural and mental health challenges.
Contribute to the development and implementation of wellbeing programmes and initiatives.
Maintain accurate records and uphold professional and ethical standards.
Participate as an integral member of the school's pastoral care and wellbeing team.
We are looking for someone who
Holds appropriate counselling qualifications and professional registration or membership with a recognised counselling body.
Has experience working with adolescents and their families.
Demonstrates strong interpersonal, communication and relationship-building skills.
Has a sound understanding of child and adolescent development, mental health and wellbeing.
Is culturally responsive and committed to Te Tiriti o Waitangi and inclusive practice.
Can work collaboratively while maintaining professional independence and confidentiality.
We offer
A supportive and collegial staff environment.
Opportunities for professional growth and development.
The chance to make a genuine impact on the wellbeing and success of young people.
Flexible working arrangements aligned with the 0.6 FTTE position.
Terms and conditions
This is a 0.6 FTTE permanent position commencing by negotiation. Remuneration will be based on qualifications and experience.
Applications
Applications should include:
A covering letter.
Curriculum Vitae.
Contact details for three referees.
For further information about the position, please contact the Principal.
Join us in helping every learner thrive, belong and succeed.

title: Teacher, Full Time Permanent
text:
We are seeking a passionate and enthusiastic teacher to join our wonderful team at the beginning of Term 1, 2027.
Effective classroom practice, a strong understanding of the Science of Learning and a collaborative approach to teaching are important to us.
We are in our fifth year of working with Ideal Learning Matters in Structured Literacy and are committed to a structured maths mastery approach through Prime Maths.
We value teachers who demonstrate integrity, build positive relationships, communicate effectively and create an inclusive classroom where every child feels valued, supported and able to succeed. We welcome teachers who respect and value each child's identity, culture and background, and build strong partnerships with families.
Our staff work collaboratively to deliver a rich and broad curriculum, guided by our vision of lifelong learning and our values of being kind and trying our best.
This position would suit a beginning teacher or someone looking to grow their teaching practice within a supportive team.
Come and join our wonderful Lumsden School team!

title: Classroom Teacher
text:
Glenbrook School is looking for a committed, enthusiastic classroom teacher to join our full primary country school in Franklin from January 2027.
We are a proactive, connected school with a strong sense of community. In 2027, we will celebrate 150 years of learning at Glenbrook. A proud history that continues to shape our future. Come and work with a collaborative, hard working team who care deeply about our learners and make a difference every day.
Our values of Mana, Ako, Manaakitanga and Whakawhanaungatanga guide how we learn, teach and care for one another. We are a Spiral of Inquiry school: curious about what matters for our learners, open to learning alongside them, and committed to taking thoughtful action that makes a difference.
We believe learning includes taking risks, making mistakes and trying again. Our mantra is “FAIL means First Attempt In Learning”. We encourage ākonga to persevere, reflect and grow in confidence as learners.
We are seeking teachers who:
build respectful, inclusive relationships with ākonga, whānau and colleagues
create engaging classrooms where learners feel a sense of belonging and are supported to achieve
are reflective, collaborative and proactive in their teaching
value te ao Māori, our local curriculum and the strengths of our country community
bring strong teaching practice and a commitment to continued learning.
bring fun and curiosity to the classroom.
At Glenbrook, we are developing a curriculum that builds the knowledge, skills and strategies our learners need, while reflecting our community and local opportunities. Teachers at all career stages, including beginning teachers, are welcome to apply

Build the culture and connections that make our school a place people want to belong. Aotearoa Infinite Academy, New Zealand's first online charter school, is a thriving community growing to 2,000 students in 2027.
To bring our goals for our learners to life, we're expanding our senior leadership team from two to six deputy principals, each leading a strategic portfolio shaped by the Golden Circle.
This is the WHO role: you'll lead how we listen to, welcome and connect with our students, staff, whānau and wider community, online and in person. You'll also lead pastoral care for Year 10.
Includes a teaching component
Start: Term 1 2027
What you'll lead
Review and voice. Run schoolwide review and evaluation, including student, whānau and staff voice surveys.
Onboarding. Lead staff onboarding, plus enrolment interviews and induction for new students and whānau.
Community engagement. Host regional meet-ups, whānau hui, learning conferences and community education evenings.
EOTC. Own the EOTC calendar, RAMS approval, policy and safety sign-off.
Staff wellbeing. Lead staff socials, wellbeing and pastoral care, pōwhiri and cultural events.
Partnerships. Grow relationships with iwi, community and partners, and oversee marketing and social media.
Year 10 pastoral. Line-manage the Year 10 deans, and cohort attendance follow-up and strategies..
*please note this is not exhaustive and may be subject to change
View our job description online for more details.
Please apply via our website in the footer, under the "Join Our Team" link.

title: Qualified Kaiako
text:
Ready for a fresh start in one of New Zealand’s most stunning locations? BestStart Three Parks is a brand-new, purpose-built centre opening in early 2027, and we're looking for a passionate Qualified Teacher to join our start up team.
Licensed for 92 tamariki, our centre will feature four thoughtfully designed classrooms, including two dedicated under 2 spaces, alongside modern facilities and brand-new resources.
Located in the heart of Central Otago, Wānaka offers an incredible lifestyle. Whether you enjoy skiing, hiking, biking, water sports, or simply want to live somewhere surrounded by mountains and lakes, this is an opportunity to combine a rewarding teaching career with an amazing place to call home.
As a kaiako, you'll play an important role in shaping our centre culture, learning environments, and philosophy from the very beginning. We have opportunities available in both our under 2s and over 2s spaces, and we're looking for someone who is collaborative, adaptable, and excited to help build something special for tamariki, whānau, and the local community.
Why choose BestStart?
At BestStart, we're committed to supporting our teachers to thrive. We offer:
Full Pay Parity
Supportive mentoring and induction programme
Learning and development through Whare Ako
Leadership development opportunities
Discounted childcare
Fully funded Teacher Certification
Subsidised health insurance*
Sick leave from your first day
Wellbeing support and EAP services
About You
You'll hold a BEd/Dip Teaching Level 7 (ECE) and current Teacher Certification, with a passion for quality teaching, Te Whāriki, and creating meaningful learning experiences for tamariki.
This is a full-time position (40 hours per week, Monday to Friday).
Ready for a new adventure? Make the move to Wānaka and help create something special at BestStart Three Parks from day one.

title: Classroom Teacher
text:
Glenbrook School is looking for a committed, enthusiastic classroom teacher to join our full-primary country school in Franklin.
We are a proactive, connected school with a strong sense of community. In 2027, we will celebrate 150 years of learning at Glenbrook, a proud history that continues to shape our future. Come and work with a collaborative, hard working team who care deeply about our learners and make a difference every day.
Our values of Mana, Ako, Manaakitanga and Whanaungatanga guide how we learn, teach and care for one another. We are a Spiral of Inquiry school. We are curious about what matters for our learners, open to learning alongside them, and committed to thoughtful action that makes a difference.
We believe learning includes taking risks, making mistakes and trying again. Our mantra of FAIL means First Attempt In Learning”. We encourage ākonga to persevere, reflect and grow in confidence as learners.
We are seeking a teacher who:
builds respectful, inclusive relationships with ākonga, whānau and colleagues
creates an engaging classroom where learners feel they belong and are supported to achieve
is reflective, collaborative and proactive in their teaching
values te ao Māori, our local curriculum and the strengths of our country community
brings strong teaching practice and a commitment to continued learning.
has a great sense of fun and can work collaboratively with our wonderful team.
At Glenbrook, we are developing a curriculum that builds the knowledge, skills and strategies our learners need, while reflecting our community and local opportunities. Teachers at all career stages, including beginning teachers, are welcome to apply.

title: Deputy Principal – Ethical Digital Fluency & Safeguarding
text:
Keep our learners safe and help them use technology, including AI, wisely. Aotearoa Infinite Academy, New Zealand's first online charter school, is a thriving community growing to 2,000 students in 2027.
To bring our goals for our learners to life, we're expanding our senior leadership team from two to six deputy principals, each leading a strategic portfolio shaped by the Golden Circle.
This is a HOW role: in a school where learning happens online, you'll lead digital citizenship, online safety and child protection, and welcome our new Year 9 students.
Includes a teaching component
Start: Term 1 2027
What you'll lead
Digital citizenship and AI. Set our AI-use guidelines and acceptable use agreements.
Safeguarding. Be our child protection lead, managing disclosures, procedures and staff training.
Online incidents. Respond to any cyberbullying and harmful digital communications, liaise with Netsafe and other partners. Use data to design pro-active programmes in order to reduce and eliminate cyber issues.
Privacy and student data. Work with IT Manager to vet platforms and ensure Privacy Act compliance.
Learning platforms. From a safeguarding perspective, collaborate with DP Curriculum, to oversee the safe student use of the LMS and learning platforms with IT.
Community education. Run online safety evenings for whānau and staff.
Year 9 pastoral. Lead transition from contributing schools, orientation, dean management and cohort attendance follow-up and strategies.
*please note this is not exhaustive and may be subject to change
View our job description online for more details.
Please apply via our website in the footer, under the "Join Our Team" link.

title: Teacher of Mathematics

visa.text: Horowhenua College is an AEWV employer.

text:
We seek an innovative and enthusiastic practitioner to join our experienced and well resourced Mathematics faculty.
The ability to teach Mathematics to senior levels is necessary. Please state speciality areas/other subjects.
Position to commence Term 1, 2027.
The terms and conditions, including base salary, for this position will be in accordance with the Secondary Teachers' Collective Agreement (CA)
https://www.education.govt.nz/school/people-and-employment/employment-agreements/collective-agreements/secondary-teachers-collective-agreement/
Horowhenua College is an AEWV employer.
The base salary for trained and registered teachers will range from Step 5, $78,768 to Step 10, $107,886 depending on applicant’s qualifications and experience. Individuals’ actual base salary will be established by a salary assessment once a role is confirmed.
The position is 40 hours per week and 52 weeks per year. The place of work is Horowhenua College, Levin

title: Curriculum Innovator: English · Mathematics · Social Sciences · Sciences
text:
Four positions · Includes a teaching component
Start: Term 1, 2027
Design the online courses our learners will remember.
Aotearoa Infinite Academy, New Zealand's first online charter school, is a thriving community growing to 2,000 students in 2027. title: Year Level Dean
text:
Be the person who knows every learner in your year level and makes sure none of them slip through.
Aotearoa Infinite Academy, New Zealand's first online charter school, is a thriving community growing to 2,000 students in 2027. To bring our goals for our learners to life, we're creating new leadership roles, including Year Level Deans. In an online school, connection doesn't happen by accident. You'll build it, so every student in your cohort feels known, supported and able to access their learning.
What you'll lead
Pastoral care Be the first point of contact for students and whānau in your year level, building strong relationships online and in person.
Access to the curriculum Identify barriers to learning, from device and connectivity issues to wellbeing and learning needs, and work with curriculum leads, teachers and learning support to remove them.
Attendance and engagement Monitor daily attendance and online engagement data, follow up quickly with students and whānau, and apply our stepped attendance response.
Early intervention Spot students at risk early, put support plans in place and refer to case management and outside agencies when needed.
Wellbeing and behaviour Respond to incidents, including online incidents, using restorative practice.
Cohort culture Run year-level check-ins, celebrations and events that build belonging across our online community.
Working with leaders Report to your pastoral Deputy Principal and contribute to our schoolwide attendance and engagement strategy.
Please view our job description online for more details: https://crimsonacademy.teamtailor.com/jobs/8534264-year-level-dean

title: Department Lead – Technology
text:
Includes a teaching component.
Start: Term 1, 2027.
Build a technology department for the way young people will live and work. Aotearoa Infinite Academy, New Zealand's first online charter school, is a thriving community growing to 2,000 students in 2027. To bring our goals for our learners to life, we're creating new leadership roles, including a Department Lead for Technology. You'll shape how our learners design, code, make and solve problems, and show what world-class technology education looks like online.
What you'll lead
Department vision. Set the direction for Technology from Year 9 to Year 13, across digital technologies, design and hard materials as relevant.
Course design. Lead innovative online courses and projects that build design thinking, computational thinking and real-world problem solving.
Pathways. Connect learning to NCEA, micro-credentials, tertiary study and industry, including partnerships with tech and design organisations.
Teaching team. Lead, coach and appraise the teachers in your department, and grow a culture of experimentation.
Assessment and achievement. Oversee assessment, moderation and achievement data, and act on what it shows.
Resourcing. Manage the department budget, software and tools, working with IT on platforms and access.
Please view our job description online for more details: https://crimsonacademy.teamtailor.com/jobs/8534267-department-lead-technology

title: Year 2 and 3 Kaiako
text:
We're Looking for someone special to join our Richmond whānau!
Are you a passionate, caring kaiako who believes relationships are at the heart of great teaching? Someone who sees the potential in every tamaiti and goes the extra mile to help them thrive?
Then you might just be the person we're looking for!
Richmond Kura is a small, vibrant kura with a huge heart, nestled in the heart of Maraenui, Napier. We are incredibly proud of our tamariki, our whānau and the beautiful culture we have created together.
At Richmond, relationships come first. Always.
We believe tamariki learn best when they feel safe, seen, heard, valued and loved. Wairua and hauora underpin everything we do, and our trauma-informed approach prioritises connection, kindness and compassion.
Our values of whanaungatanga, manaakitanga and kaitiakitanga are woven into everyday kura life.
We're looking for someone who:
genuinely loves tamariki and believes every tamaiti can succeed
builds strong, positive relationships with tamariki, whānau and colleagues
brings warmth, enthusiasm, flexibility and a great sense of humour
has sound literacy and numeracy teaching practices
embraces Te Ao Māori and honours Te Tiriti o Waitangi
is a team player, willing to learn, grow and go the extra mile.
What makes Richmond special?
We're a close-knit, supportive team who work hard, laugh often and genuinely care for one another. Our tamariki are full of personality, humour and potential, and deserve an amazing kaiako who believes in them.
We don't expect you to know everything. We do expect you to care deeply, be willing to learn and bring your whole heart to our kura.
Come and be part of something special!
Kia Tū, Kia Maia – Stand Tall, Stand Proud.

our school vision of Engage, Enrich and Empower

yeaching with high expectations in a culturally diverse community

title: Centre Leader
text:
Are you a passionate leader who believes in quality early childhood education, strong relationships, and leading alongside your team? Little Waves Early Learning Centre is seeking a full-time head kaiako to join our dedicated whānau.
This is a 5-day-a-week, hands-on leadership role with a mixture of opening and closing shifts. You will work alongside tamariki and kaiako, with allocated non-contact time for leadership and administration.
Little Waves is a 50-licensed centre, including a 10-place nursery. We create a joyful, nurturing environment where every tamaiti feels safe, valued, and empowered to learn.
Guided by Te Whāriki, Te Ara Whānui, and Te Tiriti o Waitangi, we incorporate te reo Māori, mātauranga Māori, and tikanga Māori into everyday practice. Our values guide our relationships and teaching.
About the role
Working alongside the centre manager, who oversees 2 centres, you will:
lead, mentor, and inspire kaiako
support curriculum planning, assessment, and quality teaching
build strong relationships with tamariki, whānau, and the community
support licensing compliance and continuous improvement
promote inclusive practice and positive learning outcomes.
About you:
Holds an ECE teaching qualification and current practising certificate.
Has leadership experience or be ready for the next step.
Understands Te Whāriki and value Te Tiriti o Waitangi.
Incorporates te reo Māori and tikanga Māori into practice.
Is approachable, organised, reflective, and passionate about supporting others.
What we offer:
Full pay parity.
Paid professional development.
Leadership support and non-contact time.
A collaborative team and opportunities to grow.
The chance to make a genuine difference.
Following our recent ERO journey, we are committed to continuous improvement and achieving the best outcomes for tamariki.
Lead with heart and grow with our team! Apply now with your CV and cover letter. We look forward to welcoming you into our Little Waves whānau.

title: Classroom Teacher

We are seeking an enthusiastic, innovative, and reflective teacher to join our dedicated team starting in term 1, 2027. The successful applicant will bring strong curriculum knowledge, proven expertise in literacy and numeracy and a genuine passion for seeing tamariki succeed across all learning areas. Central to this role is an ability to build positive, respectful relationships with students, whānau and colleagues, while creating a vibrant, learner-centred classroom environment.
If you are a collaborative teacher who has initiative, a growth mindset, a strong commitment to continually growing and refining your practice and is willing to contribute to the wider life of the school, we would love to hear from you!
While the exact year level is to be confirmed, please let us know your preferred area of the school to teach.

title: Classroom Teacher

visa.text: Applicants must have New Zealand residence approval in accordance with NZ Immigration requirements, as well as current New Zealand teacher registration.

text:
Located in East Auckland, Pigeon Mountain Primary School is dedicated to providing a nurturing and inclusive learning environment where every student feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. Guided by our philosophy of 'Education with a Heart', we strive to foster academic success, empathy, resilience and a lifelong love of learning.
We are seeking a passionate and dedicated teacher to join our collaborative team. We welcome applications from teachers interested in working across our primary school, particularly those with a passion for teaching and learning in the middle and senior primary years.
We are looking for teachers who are highly relational, collaborative and committed to creating engaging learning environments where all ākonga can thrive. The successful applicant will value strong relationships with students, whānau and colleagues, and will be committed to inclusive practice, high-quality teaching and supporting learners to reach their full potential.
At Pigeon Mountain Primary School, you will be part of a supportive team that values collaboration, professional growth and making a positive difference for every learner.
We are also advertising for a maternity leave cover position, with the opportunity to discuss the most suitable year level based on the strengths and experience of the successful applicants.
Applicants must have New Zealand residence approval in accordance with NZ Immigration requirements, as well as current New Zealand teacher registration.

title: Scale A Teacher
text:
We seek a scale A teacher to lead a mixed level class in the senior primary school.
What makes our school different for teachers?
To provide balance and opportunities to practise self care, we offer approximately 2 blocks of release as a syndicate every week. This enables us to reduce after school meetings and open up more opportunities for collaboration, induction and ongoing support.
In 2027, we will also provide a teacher aide in every class to support the co constructed curriculum changes and accelerate learning in Literacy and Maths.
We respect teacher professionalism and expertise. We are really proud of how we have developed our English and Maths Curriculum Frameworks to reduce teacher workload, while best supporting learners. We will embed our English and Maths curriculum framework, whilst beginning the co-constructed implementation of the science and Social Science Curriculum in 2027 based on our understanding of the neuroscience behind how the brain learns. At the same time come with the desire to question and be questioned to drive culturally responsive, collaborative improvement.
The Attitude of Gratitude (A conscious decision to give and receive a deeper expression of appreciation and acknowledgement of others. It is a positive emotion which is self replicating, elicits joyfulness, builds social relationships and has a positive effect on the well being of all).
Visiting our school is strongly recommended and making time to have a hot drink and a chat with the principal Jason Ataera or Deputy Principal Olive Masina would be warmly received.
Applications close at 3pm, Friday 30 October.
Interviews completed and the successful candidate notified by Friday 6 November.

title: Assistant Head of Mathematics
allowances: 1 PMU, 1 PMMA (1 FTMMA and 1 FT RRR for 2027)
text:
Wakatipu High School’s vision is for Aotearoa New Zealand’s best all-round education. We are looking for a great educator to join our collaborative and forward-thinking learning area and school. The successful applicant will be excited by the opportunity to deliver a future-focused and holistic education in a flexible learning environment – they will be pedagogically progressive, student-centred, have a growth mindset, form effective relationships, and be ready to contribute to the all-round education of our students.
The successful applicant will have experience delivering the New Zealand Curriculum, along with the ability to teach mathematics and/or statistics at senior levels. A background in NZ Scholarship teaching is preferred.
This appointment includes 1 fixed term RRR for 2027 (equivalent to $4,000), plus 1 fixed term MMA to support with the implementation of the refreshed curriculum and Foundational Award.
Wakatipu High School is a well-resourced, co-educational school with a growing roll of more than 1,600 students, situated in Queenstown in the stunning Wakatipu Basin.
Applications close midday on Wednesday, 28 October.

title: Guidance Counsellor
text:
As part of our Christ-centred pastoral team, you will provide professional counselling and wellbeing support that helps students flourish academically, emotionally, socially, spiritually, and personally. You will work closely with students, whānau, staff, and external agencies to ensure young people are supported, encouraged, and empowered to succeed.
About you
You will:
be a qualified counsellor with professional counselling membership or eligibility
demonstrate empathy, wisdom, integrity, and professional judgement
build trusting relationships with young people and their families
be committed to professional excellence and ongoing learning
value collaboration and contribute positively to a caring school community
support and uphold the special character and values of the school.
In this role you will:
provide professional counselling services for students
support student wellbeing, resilience, and positive mental health
assist students through challenging circumstances, including grief, trauma, and personal difficulties
partner with families and staff to develop effective support strategies
contribute to a safe, inclusive, and Christ-centred school culture.
Play a key role in pastoral care and student wellbeing initiatives. This is an opportunity to use your professional skills and faith to make a meaningful difference in the lives of young people every day.

title: Kaiako - Literacy Intervention Specialist
institute: Te Aho o Te Kura Pounamu
text:
We're seeking passionate Literacy Intervention Specialists who believe in the transformative power of literacy.
You'll deliver targeted, high-impact support to learners in Years 6–13—working online, either synchronously or asynchronously, one-on-one or in small groups. Your mission: provide intensive, wrap-around interventions that accelerate progress, build confidence, and unlock potential.
What's on offer?
5 positions: Literacy Intervention Specialists
Fixed Term: 28 January to December 2027
FTE: 1.0 (40 hours per week preferred, part-time will also be considered)
Location: Any Te Kura office nationwide
Flexible work options: Up to 2 days working from home per week
About the role
As a change-maker in this role, you'll empower ākonga to unlock the transformative power of literacy and build confidence in their own abilities. Working online—both synchronously and asynchronously—you'll provide tailored support one-on-one or in small groups. Through a three-tiered framework, you'll deliver intensive, wrap-around interventions that accelerate learning and create meaningful progress.
Across focused blocks of 6 to 24 weeks, you'll use diagnostic insights to design and teach personalised programmes that meet each learner where they are and take them further than they imagined. Your work will not only build essential literacy skills but also ignite a sense of achievement and possibility that lasts well beyond the learning.
Key responsibilities include:
Designing and delivering literacy acceleration courses
Using data to track and support ākonga progress
Facilitating Huinga Ako (Learning Advisories) weekly
Collaborating with colleagues and whānau to ensure success
About you
You are an innovative, future-focused educator who thrives on authentic learning experiences. You'll bring:
Current NZ teacher registration and practising certificate
Expertise in accelerated literacy learning approaches
Strong skills in data-informed teaching
Ability to engage and inspire ākonga and whānau
Deep understanding of the NZ Curriculum

title: Principal
text:
A wonderful opportunity to lead our well loved school in the heart of a King Country (but within the Taranaki MOE region) rural and seaside community at Waikawau has become available. Whareorino School is located thirty minutes from Mōkau and one hour from Piopio. The surrounding countryside, bush, rivers and beautiful coast create an idyllic setting for our school. The area is home to the Nuku Walk, stunning scenery, the Waikawau Beach Tunnel and great fishing and hunting. We will soon be celebrating our school centennial and we are now seeking a new principal to confidently take our school into its next century of education and service to our community.
Whareorino School is a U1 full primary school with a roll of 8 students. Our team is made up of a 0.3 release teacher, a 0.2 LSC teacher, an admin / teacher aide, a Ka Ora Ka Ako cook and grounds / cleaner role. Whareorino School is part of the ‘Tainui Cluster’ of schools who collaborate for staff professional learning and rich experiences for our students in the arts, culture and sport.
Whareorino School is known for living our Vision Statement ‘Stand Tall, Grow Strong, Reach High’. Our vision for our learners is underpinned by our school values; ‘relationships, resilience and reflection’. If you are a visionary teacher and leader, who values connection, collaboration, growth, the success of tamariki and delivering an engaging place based curriculum, we invite you to apply. Our new principal will be a people person who can form caring and supportive relationships with the staff, students and wider community. A school house is available for the successful candidate.
Visits are welcomed.
Commencing Term 1 2027.

title: NZ Qualified and Registered Teacher
text:
Experienced infant and toddler kaiako
Do you see a nappy change as a moment for connection? Notice the learning in a toddler’s repeated discovery? Know the importance of creating a supportive environment?
Nau mai haere mai, we’d love to meet you!
We’re seeking an experienced infant and toddler kaiako with a current full practising certificate to join our Te Huihuinga room.
This role will suit someone who is passionate about infant and toddler development and understands how important the early years are. You will be warm, bubbly and proactive, with leadership skills and a willingness to keep learning alongside others.
What matters to us
Whanaungatanga and manaakitanga are at the heart of your practice. You build trusting relationships where tamariki, whānau and colleagues and Kotahitanga underpins it all.
You have a strong understanding of social and emotional competence, supporting tamariki through sensitive responses, co-regulation and meaningful connection.
Responsive teaching comes naturally to you. You notice children’s cues, recognise their learning and respond thoughtfully to their interests, needs and individual rhythms. You create intentional environments that invite curiosity, exploration and growing independence.
You value meaningful rituals over simply following routines. Arrivals, kai, nappy changes and sleep become unhurried opportunities to nurture trust and belonging.
What you’ll bring
Experience teaching infants and toddlers.
A current full practising certificate.
Initiative, positive energy and thoughtful communication.
Confidence leading by example, sharing ideas and supporting colleagues.
Curiosity and openness to feedback and professional growth.
A te ao Māori lens, including confidence weaving te reo Māori and tikanga into everyday practice, would be a valued bonus.
Bring your strengths and help shape our infant and toddler space.

title: Assessment Lead - Literacy and Numeracy Intervention Programme
institute: Te Aho o Te Kura Pounamu
text:
Mō tēnei tūranga mahi | About this position
We are looking for a proactive and data-informed leader to take responsibility for assessment and learner tracking within the Accelerated Literacy and Numeracy programme. This role is central to ensuring that assessment practices drive meaningful learning outcomes and support continuous improvement.
As Assessment Lead, you will:
Lead the design and implementation of assessment processes, including the use of standardised testing tools to measure ākonga progress.
Provide strategic oversight of learner data, ensuring accurate tracking, analysis, and reporting to inform teaching and programme development.
Collaborate closely with the Programme Lead to align assessment insights with programme goals and learner pathways.
Maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders to ensure assessment information is shared in ways that support learner success.
Support kaiako in interpreting data and using it to inform responsive teaching practices.
Work in partnership with National Leaders of Learning and Kaiako Matua Literacy and Numeracy to strengthen formative and summative assessment practices to inform intervention approaches.
Contribute to reporting cycles, providing evidence-based insights that support curriculum development and decision-making.
This role requires a leader who is confident with data, committed to equity, and passionate about using assessment to empower learners and educators.
Ko koe tēnei | About you
You will bring:
New Zealand teacher registration and a current practising certificate
Strong knowledge of the English curriculum and assessment practices
A calm, inclusive, and supportive approach to teaching and pastoral care
Confidence using digital tools to connect with learners
Enthusiasm for collaborative, values driven teaching

text:
The Board of St Francis Xavier School, Tawa, invites applications for the position of Principal/Tumuaki, commencing Term 2, 2027.
St Francis Xavier School is a Catholic integrated primary school (Years 1-6) with approximately 165 learners. Founded by the Brigidine Sisters, the school is grounded in a proud tradition of faith, courage, compassion, and service. Located in Tawa, the school is known for its inclusive culture, strong sense of community, and commitment to ensuring every learner is known, valued, and supported to achieve their potential.
This is an exciting opportunity for a faith-filled and visionary leader to guide a well-established Catholic school into its next chapter. The successful candidate will embrace and strengthen the school's mission to provide a Catholic environment in which children are encouraged to develop their spiritual, academic, physical, and social potential.
The ideal applicant will:
Be a committed Catholic able to authentically lead and enhance the school's special character
Inspire excellence in teaching, learning, and student achievement
Foster a culture where every learner is supported, challenged, and encouraged to flourish
Build strong partnerships with staff, whānau, parish, Board, and the wider community
Demonstrate culturally responsive leadership and honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi
Celebrate diversity and promote inclusion
Support the professional growth and development of staff
St Francis Xavier offers dedicated staff, engaged learners, strong whānau and parish support, a vibrant multicultural community where faith, excellence, service are at the heart of school life.
A willingness and ability to participate in religious instruction appropriate to the special character of the school is a condition of appointment. The successful applicant will accept responsibility for maintaining, preserving, and enriching the Catholic special character of the school.
Applications are welcomed from leaders passionate about Catholic education and committed to making a lasting difference in the lives of young people.

title: Kaiako Kura Teina
text:
E tū te huru pango, nau mai, rāhiri mai!
Tēnei te karanga a Te Kura Kaupapa Māori o Te Rāwhitiroa ki ngā kaiako pakari.
Ko te rapu mātou i tētahi toki e mātau mārika ana ki te whakaako tauira ki te kura teina (1-8), ā, e pai ana tō mahi whakawātea kaiako mō o rātou wā wātea puta noa i te Kura Teina. Māna te hinengaro pakirehua māori e whakaihiihi kia tupu te mahira, kia tupu te aronui ki te ako. Pēnā e ngākaunui ana koe ki ngā tamariki, e mātau ana ki ngā marau katoa, e matatau ana ki te reo Māori, ā, e mārama ana ki te whakatinanatanga o Te Aho Matua o ngā KKM o Aotearoa, ko koe te momo e rapu nei mātou.
Me māori ō hakaaro, ō tikanga, tō kawe hoki i a koe. Ka mutu, ko ngā taitamariki tonu te tūāpapa, te take e tono nei koe ki tēnei tūranga kaiako wā wātea.
Mehemea e whaitake ana ēnei kupu ki a koe, he nui tō hiahia ki te whāngai i tō mātauranga ki tēnei reanga; ki te hakapakari i ō rātou pūmanawa, i ō rātou pūkenga, ā, he nanakia tō momo āhuatanga hakaako e rata atu ai rātou ki te kai i ōu ringaringa - me mutu te takaroa.
Tonoa mai āu kōrero, tō tātai pūmanawa.

Why should you work at NTK?
We have a network of 23 high quality and well-resourced Kindergartens across the region, each with their own unique character.

Teaching staff are supported by a team of Senior Education Advisors, the management team, board, and association office staff, as well as administrators in every Kindergarten.
We are a not-for-profit charity which ensures all funds go towards our children’s education.
Head Teachers work 60% contact, 40% non-contact, including an additional 40 hours per year Head Teacher release.

title: Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCO)/Learning Support Coordinator (LSC)
text:
Are you passionate about ensuring every learner can access, participate, and succeed in education? Central Regional Health School is seeking an experienced and collaborative Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCO) and Learning Support Coordinator (LSC) to lead and coordinate learning support services for students whose health or wellbeing needs impact their educational engagement and achievement.
This is an exciting opportunity to make a significant difference for young people and their whānau by ensuring equitable access to education and supporting successful pathways back into learning, training, employment, and community participation.
As our SENCO / LSC you will:
Lead the identification, coordination, and monitoring of learning support for students with diverse and complex needs.
Coordinate Individual Education Plans (IEPs) and transition planning.
Build teacher capability in inclusive, culturally responsive, and trauma-informed practice.
Work collaboratively with whānau, health professionals, enrolling schools, and community agencies.
Coordinate access to specialist services and learning support pathways.
Contribute to strategic planning and the ongoing development of inclusive school-wide practices.
Advocate for students and ensure their voice is central to decision making.
We are looking for a NZ registered teacher who:
Has successful experience supporting learners with additional learning, behavioural, health, disability, or mental health needs.
Demonstrates strong knowledge of inclusive education and learning support systems.
Builds effective partnerships with whānau and multidisciplinary teams.
Has excellent communication, organisational, and case-management skills.
Is committed to Te Tiriti o Waitangi and culturally responsive practice.
Can work independently across a geographically dispersed region.
Experience as a SENCO, Learning Support Coordinator, pastoral leader, or in specialist education settings will be highly regarded.
This position requires regular travel. Applicants must hold a full New Zealand driver's licence and have access to a registered and warranted vehicle for work-related duties.
Join us in making a meaningful difference for young people and their whānau.

title: Tumuaki Tuarua
institute: Te Kura o Ngāti Whātua ki Tāmaki
text:
E kimi ana a Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei i tētahi Tumuaki Tuarua whai pūkenga, kia tū ki Te Kura o Ngāti Whātua ki Tāmaki, tō tātou kura kaupapa Māori hou kei te pū o Tāmaki Makaurau.
He whai wāhitanga motuhake tēnei ki te whai wāhi ki te whakatupu i tētahi kura e ū pū ana ki te Ngāti Whātua Ōrākeitanga, Te Marautanga o Aotearoa me ngā wawata o tō tātou iwi. Ka mahi ngātahi koe ki te Tumuaki ki te ārahi i ngā kaupapa mātauranga mō ngā Tau 9 ki te 13, ā, ka noho tonu koe hei pouako ki te taha o ngā uri.
E kimi ana mātou i tētahi kaiārahi mātauranga whai wheako, he matatau ki te reo Māori, he tino māramatanga ki te mātauranga Māori me ngā horopaki rūmaki reo Māori, ā, e ngākau nui ana ki te tautoko i ngā uri kia eke panuku hei Māori.
Mēnā e hihiko ana koe ki te whakatupu i tētahi kura hou, ki te waihanga hoki i tētahi ara mātauranga e takea mai ana i te kaupapa Māori me ngā wawata o te iwi, nau mai, tukuna mai tō tono.

Te Puna Reo Ōkahukura was established in 2007 by Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei and is part of a long-term kaupapa of education excellence where knowledge and understanding of te reo māori me ngā tikanga are a foundation.
Te Whiwhinga Mahi
Ko te mahi a te Kaiako i Te Puna Reo Ōkahukura, he whakatupu, he whāngai hoki i te oranga tonutanga o ngā tamariki i raro i te maru o te reo Māori, o ngā tikanga Māori, me ngā mātauranga tuku iho. Mā tēnei tūranga e ū, e ora hoki te reo me ngā tikanga hei tūāpapa mō te ako, te tiaki, me te hauora o ngā tamariki. Me arero Māori te tangata e piri mai ana ki tēnei kaupapa, ka mutu, ka aromātaitia tō reo hei te wā o te uiui.
We proudly honour Full Pay Parity rates, and certificated kaiako working in kaupapa Māori immersion early learning services such as ours, are also entitled to the Waha Rumaki monthly allowance.
Ngā tino pūkenga/whēako | Essential qualifications and experience
Holds a recognised ECE or Primary teaching qualification and current NZ teacher registration. New graduates and 3rd year students are welcome to apply.
Have a passion for working with tamariki in kaupapa Māori education.
Requirements and checks
Applicants must have the right to work in New Zealand..
Safety check.

About the role
Working in collaboration with centre whānau and other centre support staff, the Centre Coordinator focuses on building adult capability and confidence.
As the Person Responsible on session, this role provides high quality support and pedagogical guidance to Playcentre whānau. The Centre Coordinator ensures sessions and programmes reflect Playcentre Philosophy and enriches children’s learning and development.

Developing whānau to be the first and best educators for their tamariki by ensuring rich, meaningful, child-led curriculum experiences

You will be confident building and maintaining strong relationships, providing guidance and solutions with a centre-focused approach.

Passion for Playcentre philosophy and empowering whānau
Course 3 of the Playcentre Education Diploma or equivalent ECE Qualification Level 4+
Confidence using technology to support learning & administration
Strong knowledge of Te Whāriki, ECE regulations, and a commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi
Hold and maintain appropriate First Aid certification
NZ residency or a valid NZ work visa
About us
Formed in 1941, Te Whānau Tupu Ngātahi o Aotearoa – Playcentre Aotearoa is a licensed early childhood education provider and charitable trust. With a philosophy of empowering ‘parents as first educators’, Playcentre seeks to empower whānau and tamariki to work, play, learn and grow together, and today has over 400 centres nationwide.

text:
The role
We are looking for a Teacher in Training, or experienced Unqualified Teacher, to join our Keas room (2-3.5 year olds) at Bear Park Remuera. Working with this age group is engaging, rewarding and fun! With ratios of at least 1:7 we allow our teachers the ability to engage in intentional and meaningful learning opportunities with small groups.
From our spacious outdoor areas to our central piazza, we’ve created an environment that is natural, transparent and inspiring for all. We focus on the many expressive languages that children use and develop throughout their early years, with our performing arts room and central and classroom ateliers encouraging children to engage in the art of dance, drama, music, art and more.
Why Bear Park?
At Bear Park we are committed to providing inspiring professional development, including paid in-service sessions held every 2 months, where all of Bear Park comes together to connect and enrich our practice. We also offer opportunities to attend external workshops and conferences, supporting our teachers to be the best they can be. With 3 hours of dedicated group planning time per room, per week, we deliver incredible, individualised programmes for each of the children in our care.
With inspiration from Reggio Emilia, our teachers have a passion for inspiring wonder, creativity, imagination and investigation, fostering children's hundred languages and unravelling their theories alongside them.
What next?
Our philosophy is grounded in relationships, curiosity and a genuine belief in the potential of every child. If you're passionate about early childhood education and want to work alongside a team that values great teaching, continuous learning and strong relationships, we'd love to hear from you.
Candidates must be a New Zealand Resident or Citizen, or hold a valid New Zealand work visa that permits full-time employment, to be considered for this position.

title: Tumuaki, Principal U5
text:
With an expected roll of 372 tamariki in 2027, Te Ahuwai Bromley is a vibrant, culturally diverse, community kura where relationships, belonging and learning are at the heart of everything we do. We are seeking an innovative and grounded Tumuaki to build on the legacy of our long-standing Principal and lead our kura into its next exciting chapter.
Our kura is grounded in the belief that strong relationships, connection and collective responsibility create outcomes where every child can thrive. Our diverse community offers our Māori, NZ European, Pasifika and Asian students enriching experiences and perspectives. We want every child to see themselves, their culture and their identity reflected, respected and valued, and to know they are an important contributor to our shared community.
Our Reggio-inspired philosophy places tamariki at the centre of learning, recognising their strengths, curiosity, creativity and agency. As an Apple Distinguished School, we embrace innovation, purposeful technology and collaborative learning to empower tamariki to explore possibilities, share their thinking and help shape their learning.
We seek a Tumuaki who will nurture these foundations, champion inclusive and culturally responsive practice, and strengthen partnerships with whānau, staff and our wider community. You will recognise the value of diverse perspectives, foster a culture of collaboration and belonging, and inspire our tamariki and kaiako to grow together.
You will lead a passionate team of 23 teaching staff and 19 support staff, united by our mission: “Achieving personal growth for all through strong community partnerships and innovative teaching and learning.”
This is an opportunity to lead a high-functioning kura with a strong sense of identity, a connected community and an ambition to keep growing.
If you believe every child belongs, every voice matters and every learner has the potential to make a difference, we would love to hear from you.

title: Principal
text:
Do you want to lead a quintessential rural New Zealand school, while still enjoying easy access to Palmerston North?
For 131 years, Makuri School has stood proud at the heart of our beautiful valley. Surrounded by native bush, our school is supported by an incredibly strong, engaged community and a dedicated Board of Trustees, deeply invested in the success of our children.
We are looking for a motivated, energetic, and passionate leader to guide our capable rural children and bring out their absolute best. If you are looking for a role where your impact is immediately visible, where every child is known personally, and where you have the autonomy to truly innovate, Makuri School is your next step.
This is an exciting opportunity for someone looking to take on their first Principal role. You will work alongside a supportive Board of Trustees that actively encourages professional learning and development. You will enjoy the freedom to lead, create, and innovate in a school where relationships truly matter.
As the Principal, you can live in the recently refurbished school house, rented at a very competitive rate. If you enjoy fishing, hunting, or tramping, this is the ideal location for you. Or, if playing pool and darts at the local Country Club, joining a local book club, or attending the much-anticipated Annual Social Club event are more your thing, you will quickly find Makuri is the place to be!
We want a leader whose style aligns with our MAKURI values:
Motivated and adaptable – Ready to embrace the rewards of rural education.
Kind and united – Building strong relationships with families and the community.
Resourceful and involved – Eager to be a visible, active part of our close-knit valley.
Ready to make a genuine, lasting impact? Apply now to lead Makuri School into its next exciting chapter.

title: Junior School Kaiako

Solid NZC and pedagogical knowledge: Current, relevant NZC understanding with a commitment to alignment with the Weston School Teaching and Learning Framework.

Inclusivity: A genuine drive to know your learners well and foster meaningful partnerships with whānau.
What we’re looking for in a colleague:
Team spirit: Kind, reliable, reflective, and eager to collaborate.
Curiosity and adaptability: Someone who loves learning, adapts smoothly to change, and doesn't take themselves too seriously.

title: Principal | Tumuaki U5

text:
Taumarunui is a welcoming district known for its natural environment and a strong sense of community. Set under Mt Ruapehu, and on the upper Whanganui River, Taumarunui offers affordable housing, an abundance of outdoor activities and sports, and easy access to Lake Taupo. Our approach places Pacific identities, languages, cultures and ways of knowing at the heart of learning, while honouring Te Tiriti o Waitangi and our responsibilities to tangata whenua. Our values of Alofa (Love and Commitment), Tautua (Service and Responsibility), and Fa’aaloalo (Respect) guide how we teach, lead and care for our young people.
The successful applicant will teach across a range of core curriculum areas in Years 9–10 and contribute to an engaging, integrated junior programme. We are looking for a teacher who builds strong relationships with rangatahi and whānau and believes deeply in the potential of Māori and Pacific learners.

Can confidently teach across Year 9–10 core NZ curriculum areas.
Demonstrate strong culturally responsive and relational practice.
Are committed to PASS’s Special Character and Pacific-centred approach to education.
Hold, or are eligible to hold, a current NZ practising certificate.
Work collaboratively and bring energy, creativity and high expectations to junior learning.
Are biliterate speakers of Samoan and English – an advantage, but not essential.
Are biliterate speakers of Te Reo Māori or other Pacific languages - an advantage, but not essential.

title: Physiotherapist
text:
Rosehill School is seeking a physiotherapist who is passionate about working with children and young adults with special needs. This role would suit an experienced physiotherapist or a new graduate with a strong interest in paediatrics.
Rosehill School supports students aged 5–21 years across our base school, 14 satellite units within mainstream schools, and a transition unit for students aged 18–21.
Our students have a diverse range of needs, including Cerebral Palsy and Autism. We are a multicultural school that values and celebrates diversity.
You will join a large, supportive therapy team including Occupational Therapists, Physiotherapists, Speech Language Therapists and Psychologists.
The role involves:
Working collaboratively with class teams, whānau and other therapy disciplines.
Supporting students to access the curriculum, participate in school life and develop physical independence.
Upskilling teaching and support staff in best practice.
Managing a varied caseload across multiple school sites.
Contributing to school-wide improvement initiatives.
Engaging in professional development opportunities.
We are looking for someone who:
Has a strong interest in neurodevelopmental paediatrics and working with children with special needs.
Has excellent interpersonal and collaborative skills.
Has a positive, flexible and solutions-focused approach.
Can effectively manage their time and work across multiple sites.
Has an interest or experience in postural management, wheelchairs and seating.
Is committed to evidence-based, neuro-affirming practice.
Travelling between sites is essential, with mileage reimbursement provided for use of a personal vehicle.
Remuneration is based on the Ministry of Education Kaiārahi i te Reo and Therapists’ Collective Agreement.

title: Kaiako Years 7 & 8
text:
Ngākōroa School has an opportunity for a Year 7 and 8 kaiako starting at the beginning of Term 1 2027. If you enjoy teaching rangatahi as they develop a love of learning, self-efficacy and independence, we would love to hear from you.
This is a unique opportunity to co-teach with an experienced hāpori leader with strong culturally responsive practice within a two-class composite hub. With full-time kaiawhina support, the team create engaging, differentiated learning opportunities that respond to strengths, cultures and learning needs of our rangatahi.
Previous co-teaching experience is not essential but a collaborative mindset, and commitment to inclusive, relationship-based practice are.
Our school is a central part of the diverse and growing community in Auranga (Drury). We have an integrated, conceptual approach to the curriculum alongside structured teaching in literacy and mathematics. We are guided by our vision, Kawea te Mātauranga ki te Whaiao, ki te Ao Mārama – Bringing Learning to Life, in everything we do.
Ngākōroa has a strong staff culture, supportive leadership, community connections and relationships with local iwi. As a growing kura with solid foundations, we offer opportunities to contribute, innovate and grow professionally.
We are looking for kaiako wanting to contribute to our kura and add their strengths to ours. Units for school-wide leadership responsibilities are negotiable around your strengths (such as Sports Co-ordinator, Garden to Table). If you are interested contributing to the leadership please state in your cover letter.
Visits to our kura are warmly encouraged. We would love to hear from you!

title: Counsellor (Term time only)
institute: Christchurch Girls' High School -Te Kura o Hine Waiora
text:
We are seeking a relational, dedicated, and professional guidance counsellor to provide student-centred care and responsive pastoral support for rangatahi. In this role, you will help young people navigate social, emotional, and behavioural challenges within a culturally safe and restorative environment.
Key responsibilities
Deliver confidential, one-on-one counselling for ākonga.
Manage student risk assessments, safety planning, and crisis interventions.
Collaborate effectively with our pastoral team (including Deans and senior leadership), whānau, and external specialist support services.
Maintain accurate, timely clinical and administrative records in line with school and professional standards.
The successful candidate will bring
A recognised tertiary counselling qualification and current NZAC (or equivalent) registration (full or provisional).
Proven experience counselling adolescents in an educational or youth mental health setting.
High empathy, person-centred practice, sound clinical judgement, and strong professional ethics.
Excellent communication skills, strong digital capability (including Excel and custom software), and strong administrative organisation.
High personal accountability, initiative, and a proactive approach to identifying student needs and ensuring thorough follow-through.
You will understand that school counselling is deeply relational work requiring consistency, calm, and active engagement. You take pride in creating a safe, positive space for young people while navigating a busy school environment with professional judgement.
Position details
Type: Permanent, term-time only (30 hours per week)
Start Date: 27 January 2027
Closing Date: Midnight, Sunday 1 November 2026
To apply
Applications must be submitted via the Christchurch Girls’ High School | Te Kura o Hine Waiora website.

title: Tumuaki, Kura-ā-iwi, U4
institute: Te Kura ā Iwi o Whakatupuranga Rua Mano
text:
Ko te reo pōwhiri tēnei o Te Kura ā-iwi o Whakatupuranga Rua Mano mō te tūranga tumuaki. Ka ārahi i te kura kia ū, kia tutuki i ngā mātāpono i whakatōngia, nō te kaupapa o Whakatupuranga Rua Mano.
He mea ārahi te kura e te iwi, e te whānau . Ko ngā mātāpono tekau o te kura ka noho hei tūāpapa mō ngā mahi katoa. Ko tā te kura, he poipoi i ngā tamariki kia Māori te titiro ki te ao, kia whai i te ara ā Tāwhaki.
Ko ngā āhuatanga o te tumuaki:
Ka whakatauira i ngā mātāpono o te kura, i roto mai i te kura, i waho atu o te kura, ka mutu, i roto i ngā mahi katoa.
He mātanga reo Māori e āhei ana ki te whakatakoto me te whakatinana i ngā rautaki hei whakawhanake i te kounga, i te matatau me te rere o te reo Māori puta noa i te kura. Tamariki mai, kaimahi mai, whānau mai.
He māramatanga ki te mana o te whānau, e whai hua ai ngā tamariki i roto i ngā mahi katoa.
He pūkenga rawa ki te whakarite rautaki e tutuki pai ai i ngā hiahia me ngā matea ako o ia tamaiti me tōna whānau.
Ka mōhio ki ngā tātai kōrero o Whakatupuranga Rua Mano me Te Kotahitanga o ngā Iwi ki te Tonga - Te Āti Awa, Ngāti Raukawa te Au ki te Tonga, Ngāti Toa Rangatira.
He kanohi kitea ia e ngā whānau o te kura, e te hapori, e ngā marae o Te Kotahitanga o ngā Iwi.
He pūkenga ki te ārahi, ki te whakakotahi, ki te whakahihiko i te wairua o ngā kaiako me ngā kaimahi o te kura.
He pūkenga whakahaere kura. Ko ngā mahi tahua, whakaū i nga kaupapa here, whakahaere rawa, hangarau matahiko me te whakatutuki i ngā rautaki.

title: Learning Support Coordinator / Structured Literacy teacher
text:
We are seeking an experienced, passionate and fully certificated teacher to join our team as our Learning Support Coordinator (LSC) / Structured Literacy Teacher.
Following the retirement of our long-serving SENCO/LSC, we have an exciting opportunity for a skilled educator to lead and strengthen our inclusive learning practices, while making a meaningful difference for learners who require additional support.
This is a key leadership position within our school, combining learning support coordination, evidence-informed structured literacy intervention, and the development of inclusive teaching practices across our learning community.
What you'll do
Lead Inclusive Practice: Be an active member of our school's Leadership Team, helping shape a school-wide approach to inclusive education and equitable learning opportunities.
Make a Difference Through Structured Literacy: Plan and deliver explicit, systematic, evidence-informed literacy interventions that respond to individual learning needs and accelerate progress.
Intervene Early: Identify learning needs and coordinate timely, targeted support to help ākonga experience success.
Strengthen Teaching Practice: Work alongside classroom teachers and teacher aides, sharing expertise and building collective capability to respond to diverse learning needs.
Build Strong Partnerships: Develop positive, collaborative relationships with parents and whānau, ensuring they are informed, involved and supported throughout their child's learning journey.
Coordinate Learning Support: Work collaboratively with staff, whānau and external agencies to ensure learning support is well coordinated, responsive and effective.
What we're looking for
We are looking for an educator who:
Is an experienced, fully certificated teacher with a strong commitment to inclusive education.
Has demonstrated expertise in delivering structured literacy interventions.
Understands diverse learning needs and can use assessment information to plan, monitor and evaluate targeted support.
Has strong communication, relationship-building and collaborative leadership skills.
Is passionate about building teacher capability and creating positive outcomes for all learners.
If you are an enthusiastic, collaborative educator who believes every learner deserves the opportunity to thrive, we would love to hear from you.

title: Te Reo Māori Teacher
text:
Kei te hunga e aroha nui ana ki ngā rangatahi me tō tātou reo Māori me ōna Tikanga, tēnā koutou.
Kei te rapu mātou i tētahi kaiako reo Māori hei kawe i te whakaako me te mātauranga Māori ki tō mātou kura, arā, ko te Kāreti o Maungakiekie. Ko Te Puakiekie te whare e karanga nei
He tūranga poto tēnei nā te mea, ka whai tō mātou kaiako i tōna tohu paerua. E wātea ana tūranga ki te hunga kua roa nei e takahi ana i te ara o te mātauranga Māori.
Me manawera te kaitono ki te whakaaweawetanga o ngā ākonga Māori, me mārama hoki ia ki ngā tikanga o te NZC. Ka whai wāhi atu te kaitono ki ngā kaupapa Māori i tō mātou kura me ētahi mahi marau-turuki pērā i te hākinakina.
Ki te hiahia koe ki te tono, ka tukua mai tōu tātai pūmanawa me tētahi reta ōkawa hei whakamōhio atu ki a mātou āu pukenga me āu wheako o mua.
Nau mai, haere mai ki tō mātou kura. Tūtaki mai ki tō mātou tīma, ki ā mātou ākonga hoki.
One Tree Hill College is looking to employ an experienced, dynamic and highly motivated teacher and leader who can teach Te Reo Māori to junior and senior levels, and potentially lead our Māori Department.
This is a fixed term role for 2027 whilst our Whaea is on study leave completing further studies towards her Masters of Secondary School Leadership.
The role carries with it 2 fixed term management units and 2 middle management allowances.
This is an exciting opportunity to be a part of an inclusive and very supportive staff, and teach at our well-resourced and recently redeveloped college.

title: Kaiako for Akomanga Teina (Years 0–3)
text:
He iti Pioke, nō Rangaunu, he au tōna!
E kimi ana Te Kura o Waihārara i tētahi kaiako ngākau mahana, ngākau hihiko hoki hei whakaako i te Akomanga Teina, tō mātou akomanga rumaki reo Māori mō ngā tamariki Tau 0–3.
He tūranga wā-katoa, wā-whāiti tēnei hei whakakapi i tētahi kaiako i te whakamatuatanga mātua, mai i te 2 o Hui-tanguru ki te 1 o Hereturikōkā 2027.
Me whai rēhitatanga kaiako me tētahi tiwhikete whakaako whaimana. He mea nui te āhei ki te whakaako mā te reo Māori, te reo matatini me te pāngarau tūāpapa, me te whakawhanaunga ki ngā tamariki me ngā whānau. E pōwhiri ana hoki mātou i ngā kaiako e whakapakari tonu ana i tō rātou reo Māori, ā, e āhei ana ki te tautoko i tō mātou akomanga rumaki.
E rapu ana mātou i tētahi kaiako mahi ngātahi, ngāwari hoki, e whakarato ana i ngā wheako ako ā-ringa, kauawhi hoki, ā, e whakaū ana i ngā uara o te kura: Ako, Kaitiakitanga me Rangatiratanga.
Te Kura o Waihārara is a small, welcoming Kura ā-Iwi in Te Hiku o Te Ika, Far North. We seek a warm, collaborative kaiako for our Years 0–3 Māori immersion classroom.
Applicants must be registered teachers with a current practising certificate. Confidence teaching through te reo Māori, foundational literacy and pāngarau, and a commitment to culturally responsive, inclusive, hands-on learning are important. We welcome applicants developing their reo who can effectively support learning in our immersion setting.
This full-time, fixed-term role covers parental leave from 2 February to 1 August 2027; the incumbent is expected back on Monday 2 August.
This vacancy is being readvertised. Previous applicants remain under consideration and need not reapply.

title: Specialist Science/Classroom Teacher

visa.text: Applicants must have NZ residence.

text:
Commencing 28 January 2027.
We are a well-resourced, innovative and dynamic school located in beautiful East Auckland. We provide an holistic and trans-disciplinary curriculum for our 11 – 13 year old students who thrive in a positive, inclusive and diverse learning environment. We have a strong values programme and foster a culture of kindness.
We require a highly effective, motivated and collaborative Science Specialist teacher who will be working in well-resourced science facilities. You would be working closely with a second Specialist Science teacher.
A good knowledge of the Science curriculum and the ability to make connections with other learning areas are essential. An understanding of the Nature of Science and the ability to develop scientifically literate students by developing science capabilities is a prerequisite. A passion for leading students through the Science Fair process would be an advantage.
Positive classroom management, cultural competence and contribution to the corporate life of the school are essential.
Join our highly regarded school and work alongside a supportive and collegial team that delivers dynamic and innovative programmes. We offer exciting opportunities for professional growth and leadership.
Possible MU for Science curriculum leadership (please state all curriculum strengths).
Applicants must have NZ residence.

title: Qualified kaiako for our preschool room
text: We are looking for a permanent qualified ECE teacher for our preschool. A creative and passionate teacher who can bring a new spark with fresh ideas and creativity, with strong understanding of planning and implementation of curriculum under Te Whāriki, and who is a supportive team player keen to work collaboratively to provide high-quality learning for our tamariki.

title: Kaiārahi (Leader)
text:
Elements Nature Based Play is on a mission to get tamariki back outside spending more time in nature. At Elements we allow for ample unstructured playtime in the great outdoors, leading to creative social adventures between the tamariki. Our curriculum inspires tamariki to think independently and openly.
We are seeking a kaiārahi (leader) to join our team that offers sessions during the school and summer holidays. Days are generally 8.30am to 4pm in our two locations in Westmorland and Marshlands. Currently we provide programmes for tamariki aged 5 to 13. This is a casual contract position.
A kaiārahi will co-lead daily programming with a fellow kaiārahi and potentially junior kaiārahi as needed by enrolments. Kaiārahi are responsible for the safety of all participating tamariki, and assisting with projects and activities throughout the day. This person will be responsible for checking in with caregivers at the start and and end of the programme and communicating with them about the specific needs of the tamariki (allergies, behavourial needs, etc.).
Training, daily programmes, curriculum, policy documents, health and safety documentation is provided.

We have flexibility within our timetable and are interested in teachers with strengths in English, Mathematics, Social Studies, Science, Technology or Performing Arts. We are a small school with big ambitions, where our ākonga are at the heart of everything we do.
Meaningful Teaching: The opportunity to truly know your learners and make a difference to their learning and wellbeing.
A Supportive Team: A collaborative staff and leadership team invested in the success of our teachers and students.
A Culture of Balance: We value staff wellbeing and recognise the importance of balancing professional commitments with life outside the classroom.
Opportunities to Grow: We support professional learning and encourage staff to contribute to the wider life of the school.

We are looking for a teacher who demonstrates culturally responsive and relational practice, builds positive relationships and is confident teaching across different curriculum areas. Experience teaching within the New Zealand Curriculum is important.
Position details
This is a full-time, board-funded, fixed-term position for the 2027 school year, commencing Term 1. The position supports the transition to our revised curriculum and staffing structure.
Applicants must hold current New Zealand teacher registration and a practising certificate, and have the legal right to work in New Zealand.

text:
Taumarunui is a friendly, welcoming district known for its relaxed lifestyle, beautiful natural surroundings, and a strong sense of community. Set amongst rolling hills and on the stunning Whanganui River, Taumarunui is a small town setting, but with all the services of the city.

The school’s strong connection with its community creates a warm, inclusive atmosphere, and its smaller class sizes and both collaborative and structured learning approaches, allows teachers to build meaningful relationships and make a real difference for our students.

text:

A supportive and collegial team environment.
Opportunities for professional development and specialist training.
The chance to make a lasting impact in the lives of ākonga and their communities.

title: Centre Coordinator – Te Kauwhata Playcentre

visa.text: NZ residency or a valid NZ work visa

text:
11 hours per week | Part-time | Starting 30 November 2026
Monday 9.15am – 1.15pm
Wednesday and Friday 9.15am – 12.45pm.
Permanent position during term time only.
About the role
Working in collaboration with centre whānau and other centre support staff, the Centre Coordinator focuses on building adult capability and confidence.
As the Person Responsible on session, this role provides high quality support and pedagogical guidance to Playcentre whānau. The Centre Coordinator ensures sessions and programmes reflect Playcentre Philosophy and enriches children’s learning and development.
Duties include, but are not limited to:
developing whānau to be the first and best educators for their tamariki by ensuring rich, meaningful, child-led curriculum experiences
role-modelling and supporting the delivery of high quality, whānau-led sessions
providing advice and support to centre whānau focusing on curriculum, adult education and health and safety to support session delivery
ensure sessions meet regulatory and legislative requirements including Health and Safety obligations
recognise the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and how they relate to Playcentre and actively engage in promotion of Māori cultural values
About you
You will be confident building and maintaining strong relationships, providing guidance and solutions with a centre-focused approach.
You will also have:
passion for Playcentre philosophy and empowering whānau
course 3 of the Playcentre Education Diploma or equivalent ECE Qualification Level 4+
confidence using technology to support learning & administration
strong knowledge of Te Whāriki, ECE regulations, and a commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi
hold and maintain appropriate First Aid certification
NZ residency or a valid NZ work visa
About us
Formed in 1941, Te Whānau Tupu Ngātahi o Aotearoa – Playcentre Aotearoa is a licensed early childhood education provider and charitable trust. With a philosophy of empowering ‘parents as first educators’, Playcentre seeks to empower whānau and tamariki to work, play, learn and grow together, and today has over 400 centres nationwide.

title: Learning Support Coordinator
text:
Broadgreen Intermediate is seeking an exceptional teacher to take on the pivotal role of Learning Support Coordinator in our kura. Following the retirement of our long-serving SENCO, this is an exciting opportunity to help shape the next phase of learning support at Broadgreen.
We are looking for a highly effective classroom practitioner with a strong understanding of quality teaching and learning, and inclusive practice. You will understand how strong classroom practice can be adapted to ensure every ākonga can participate, progress and experience success.
Working alongside teachers, learners, whānau, learning assistants, school leaders and external agencies, you will help identify learner needs early, coordinate appropriate support, strengthen classroom practice, build staff capability and develop effective, sustainable school-wide systems.
The successful applicant will be relational, collaborative, organised and solution-focused, with the ability to use data well, navigate complex learning needs and contribute confidently at a leadership level.
The position carries 1 Management Unit for leadership and day-to-day management of Broadgreen’s Learning Assistant team.
A current full practising certificate and relevant teaching qualification are required for the LSC role.

title: Castle Hill Outdoor Education Centre Operations Manager
text:
Located in Christchurch, St Andrew’s College is an independent, co-educational school offering top quality education, cultural, arts and sporting activities to over 1,600 day and boarding students from pre-school to Year 13. St Andrew’s has a proud Presbyterian heritage and long tradition of academic, sporting, cultural and leadership excellence. While tradition and history are fundamental to the spirit of St Andrew’s, the school has its sights firmly fixed on the future.
The College seeks an applicant with significant experience in the leadership of Outdoor Education. Based at Castle Hill, the Operations Manager will lead the College’s fully operational outdoor education centre and programme. The Operations Manager will lead and develop a high functioning team of instructors who will be responsible for delivering outdoor programmes within the Castle Hill Basin and beyond to students across the College and specialised programmes to senior students, such as Silver and Gold Duke of Edinburgh.
Reporting to the Deputy Principal – Operations and Co-curricular, responsibilities include strategic planning, programme design, staff management, recruitment and professional development, management of facilities and equipment, health and safety and other programme offerings. The expectation is that the role is based on site at Castle Hill while the centre and programmes are in operation.
This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced leader in Outdoor Education seeking to impact positively on the lives of young people and to join a dynamic, forward-thinking team in a middle leadership position. St Andrew’s College is committed to the ongoing professional development of its staff and offers significant benefits in addition to a supportive working environment.
This is a permanent, full-time position commencing 18 January 2027, or by negotiation.

title: Mathematics Head of Faculty
allowances: 2 MU, Eligible for the Teaching Bonding Scheme - worth $40,000 over 5 years
text:
Due to the retirement of the incumbent, Ōtaki College is seeking a Head of Faculty for our Mathematics Department. This full-time, permanent position will commence in Term 1, 2027.
About us
Ōtaki College is a Year 7-13, vibrant, culturally responsive co-educational school. We serve a connected and supportive coastal community. We are a Positive Behaviour for Learning and Huakina Mai School with a roll of approximately 450 students.
About the role
We are seeking a collaborative educational leader to steer ongoing curriculum innovation and champion positive outcomes for all rangatahi. The ideal candidate brings strong organizational skills and a commitment to fostering whanaungatanga and restorative learning practices. The role involves oversight of the mathematics curriculum from Year 7 onwards. The Mathematics Head of Faculty is assisted by 2 Assistant HoFs who assist in the organisation of the junior Mathematics curriculum. The ability to teach both Level 3 Statistics and Level 3 Calculus will be an advantage. The position includes a teaching load of 4 classes, which will be allocated according to the strengths and preferences of the successful applicant.
This role is eligible for the Teaching Bonding Scheme, worth $40,000 over 5 years.

title: Deputy Principal (5MU) - Leadership Opportunity
text:
Are you an experienced and passionate educational leader looking to make a real impact? Omanu School, a thriving primary school in Mount Maunganui, is seeking a dynamic Deputy Principal (5MU) to join our leadership team.
About the role
Working closely with the principal and leadership team, you will play a key role in driving curriculum innovation, student achievement, and staff professional growth, while fostering an inclusive culture and promoting the wellbeing of our Omanu School Whānau.
What we’re looking for
We seek a leader who is:
emotionally intelligent, building strong, trust-based relationships with kaiako, tamariki, and whānau
an inspiring communicator committed to student success and wellbeing
experienced in curriculum leadership with a strong understanding of the NZC and pedagogical implementation
culturally responsive, with a demonstrated commitment to Te Tiriti-led practice
experienced leading across Phases 1 and 2, with Phase 1 expertise being a strong advantage
strategic, creative, and proactive in contributing to school vision
able to lead with empathy, accountability, and agility
a collaborative team player with a sense of humour and a growth mindset.
Why join us?
Omanu School offers a strong sense of community, high expectations, and a balanced learning experience for all our tamariki. Join a supportive, fun, and progressive environment where you can lead, inspire, and grow.
Ready to take the next step? We encourage applicants to arrange a school visit by contacting our office at [phone: see Gazette].

title: Part-time Teacher. Classroom release, Technology and EOTC
text:
1 or 2 positions - 0.2-0.6 negotiable.
Looking for variety, a supportive team and opportunities to share your strengths?
Pārāwai School is a well-resourced Years 0 to 8 school in Thames, gateway to the Coromandel. We are seeking enthusiastic, adaptable teachers to join our experienced, collegial team.
We have a range of teaching opportunities that may be shared between two applicants or combined to create a larger part-time role. title: Leader of Learning Support (SENCO)
text:
Tikipunga High School is seeking a passionate, capable and collaborative leader to lead our high-performing, well-resourced learning support department. Commencing Term 1 2027.
