The ability to lead school-wide inclusive practices, coordinate specialist services and manage learning support systems and resources is essential.

title: Specialist Teacher of Literacy
text:
Freyberg High School is seeking an experienced and passionate literacy specialist to help us build and deliver a responsive, evidence-informed literacy programme for ākonga in Years 9 to 13. This is a permanent, full-time position commencing Term 1, 2027.
This is an exciting opportunity for a skilled practitioner who wants to make a measurable difference for learners and contribute to the development of a sustainable, school-wide approach to literacy. We welcome applications from primary-trained or secondary-trained teachers who can demonstrate strong specialist literacy knowledge and experience.
Key responsibilities
Plan and deliver explicit, systematic literacy instruction that responds to identified learner needs.
Use assessment information to identify needs, group learners, monitor progress and evaluate the impact of interventions.
Support students to strengthen the reading, writing, vocabulary and language-comprehension skills required for success across the curriculum.
Help students build the literacy capabilities and confidence needed to access NCEA and the literacy co-requisite.
Contribute specialist knowledge to the continuing development of effective literacy practice across our kura.
Build strong, mana-enhancing relationships with ākonga, whānau and colleagues.
A willingness to teach within another subject area also – please state specialist subject area(s).
What you'll bring
A recognised teaching qualification and current New Zealand teacher registration.
Specialist knowledge of literacy acquisition and effective literacy intervention.
Experience using explicit, evidence-informed approaches to teaching reading and writing.
The ability to diagnose literacy needs and design differentiated programmes in response.
A sound understanding of Structured Literacy and the Science of Learning.
Confidence using data to track progress and demonstrate the impact of teaching and intervention.
An inclusive and culturally responsive approach that recognises the strengths, identities and aspirations of every learner.
Strong interpersonal skills and a genuinely collaborative, team-focused approach.
The adaptability, initiative and enthusiasm required to help build a new programme.

title: Centre Coordinator - Queenstown Playcentre

visa.text: NZ residency or a valid NZ work visa.

text:
23 hours per week | Part-time | Starting 25 January 2027
Monday from 9:30am to 3pm.
Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday 9:15am to 2:15pm.
Permanent position during term time only.
About the role
Working in collaboration with centre whānau and other centre support staff, the Centre Coordinator focuses on building adult capability and confidence.
As the Person Responsible on session, this role provides high-quality support and pedagogical guidance to Playcentre whānau. The Centre Coordinator ensures sessions and programmes reflect Playcentre Philosophy and enriches children’s learning and development.
Duties include, but are not limited to:
developing whānau to be the first and best educators for their tamariki by ensuring rich, meaningful, child-led curriculum experiences
role-modelling and supporting the delivery of high quality, whānau-led sessions
providing advice and support to centre whānau focusing on curriculum, adult education and health and safety to support session delivery
ensure sessions meet regulatory and legislative requirements including Health and Safety obligations
recognise the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and how they relate to Playcentre and actively engage in promotion of Māori cultural values.
About you
You will be confident building and maintaining strong relationships, providing guidance and solutions with a centre-focused approach.
You will also have:
passion for Playcentre philosophy and empowering whānau
course 3 of the Playcentre Education Diploma or equivalent ECE Qualification Level 4+
current First Aid Certificate or willingness to complete
confidence using technology to support learning & administration
strong knowledge of Te Whāriki, ECE regulations, and a commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi
hold and maintain appropriate First Aid certification
NZ residency or a valid NZ work visa.
About us
Formed in 1941, Te Whānau Tupu Ngātahi o Aotearoa – Playcentre Aotearoa is a licensed early childhood education provider and charitable trust. With a philosophy of empowering ‘parents as first educators’, Playcentre seeks to empower whānau and tamariki to work, play, learn and grow together, and today has over 400 centres nationwide.

text:

text:

Close to half of our learners identify as Māori, and te ao Māori is woven into learning through place-based programmes and a local curriculum.

Meaningful impact.
Supportive team.
Professional development.

text:
We are seeking a teacher who is passionate about teaching and learning, who has excellent relational skills and sound curriculum knowledge.

To apply for this position, please use the vacancy link. The link is also available on our school website.

title: Learning Support Coordinator
text:
We are seeking an experienced New Zealand registered teacher to join our team as a Learning Support Coordinator (LSC).
This is a permanent, full-time position beginning on 2 February 2027.
The successful applicant will work closely with staff, learners, whānau and external agencies to ensure students with additional learning needs receive timely appropriate support. You will contribute to a vital network dedicated to improving learning support outcomes across our school community.
The successful applicant should have recent experience working in Phase 1 and Phase 2 areas of a school with proven ability to support diverse learners and have a strong understanding of inclusive education practices. Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills are also essential for effective collaboration with staff, whānau, external agencies and other stakeholders.
This role offers an excellent opportunity to advocate for students with diverse learning needs and make a meaningful difference in their lives.

title: PE and Health teacher
text:

Ability to teach outdoor education would be an advantage.

title: Scale A teacher - Senior School
text:
Rotokauri School is a full primary on the outskirts of Hamilton. Due to promotion we have a vacancy in the senior area of our school (Year 6 & 7), but this is negotiable.
We require a positive, enthusiastic teacher who is committed to providing high quality teaching and learning for our tamariki.
The successful applicant will have sound curriculum knowledge and experience in using a wide range of strategies to support diverse learners. Strengths in literacy and numeracy are essential, as is being a reflective teacher who works collaboratively with others and has the ability to build strong relationships with students. A sense of humour would be highly advantageous. Unit allowances negotiable for leadership responsibilities.

title: Classroom Teacher: 2027 Start, Permanent
text:
Are you looking for a teaching role that allows you to grow? Is a fun and caring, team environment what you are looking for? Is working with motivated, kind and respectful learners important to you? Do you prefer to take your CRT as whole days, with the opportunity to work from home when possible?
Then Goodwood is the school for you! Come and see why we are a 2026 Educational Excellence Award winner and 2025 winners of the Vitae Workplace Wellbeing Award!
One of our talented team is relocating overseas so we are looking for a caring and capable teacher to work with our amazing explorers! Classroom level Year 3 and 4 OR Year 5 and 6 (by negotiation).
We will nourish you with high quality professional learning, daily fresh fruit and snacks, stylish merchandise and a proper coffee machine! All of this in an idyllic rural setting at a very well resourced school.
This can be a full time or 0.8 position for the right applicant.
Our school is a U5 school with a roll of 430 set in park-like grounds 5 minutes from Cambridge and 15 minutes from Hamilton.
The teacher we are looking for will be able to:
Build effective, warm and culturally responsive learning relationships with learners, their whānau and staff
Engage learners through relevant, innovative and high quality classroom management
Ensure EVERY child in their class gets a great learning experience every day
Work collegially and collaboratively.
An understanding of explicit teaching practices along with the ability to teach literacy with a scope and sequence approach is an expectation. We can provide high quality professional learning opportunities in this area.

title: Year 3&4 Classroom Teacher
text:
We are a state-integrated Catholic Years 1–8 primary school seeking an enthusiastic and committed teacher to work full‑time in our Year 3 & 4 class, covering extended parental leave for all of the 2027 school year.
We are a warm, inclusive staff who would love to welcome you into our Catholic school community. We value collegiality, shared purpose, and a genuine commitment to nurturing the whole child.
We are looking for a teacher who is adaptable and responsive, and who understands and values the diverse cultures, strengths, and learning needs of our tamariki. Strong curriculum knowledge in literacy and mathematics is expected, along with a strengths‑based and restorative behaviour management approach that supports positive relationships, learning and student wellbeing. Many of our staff have trained in Better Start Literacy.
A commitment to our school’s Catholic special character, the Gospel values and culturally responsive practice, that guide our relationships and learning is essential.
Staff are expected to recognise and respect the school’s Catholic character and to participate fully in the life of the school, in a manner that supports religious instruction and school liturgies.
This fixed term position commences Monday 18th January 2027 giving time to come into school, spend time setting up then the first day of school for students Monday 1st February 2027.

title: Health and Physical Education Teacher
text:
Hillcrest High School is seeking an enthusiastic and committed Health and Physical Education Teacher to join our vibrant, collaborative and passionate faculty.
We are particularly interested in hearing from someone with experience teaching Health Education at both junior and senior levels, who has a genuine passion for Health as a subject and a commitment to delivering engaging, meaningful and relevant learning experiences.
We are looking for a teacher who is passionate about Health Education and its role in helping young people develop critical thinking skills, explore important health issues, challenge perspectives and make informed decisions. A genuine interest in Health as a subject and a commitment to engaging students in learning that connects to their lives and the world around them is essential.
Alongside Health Education, the successful applicant will contribute to our Physical Education programme, supporting students to develop movement skills, confidence and an appreciation of the role physical activity plays in lifelong wellbeing.
You will be joining a vibrant and enthusiastic team that values collaboration, shared ideas and a genuine commitment to student learning. We are looking for someone who brings energy, initiative and a willingness to contribute to the ongoing development of Health and Physical Education within our faculty.

title: Specialist teacher CRT (0.8)
text:

The ideal candidate will have strong specialist capabilities in The Arts or Physical Education and a proven ability to design innovative, hands-on learning experiences. You will be responsible for building mana-enhancing relationships with ākonga and maintaining excellent continuity of learning while regular classroom teachers take their release.

NZ Registered Teacher with a current practising certificate.
Deep curriculum knowledge in your specialist subject area(s).
Strong classroom management strategies across various age groups.
A collaborative mindset to work seamlessly alongside regular classroom teachers.

title: Music Specialist Teacher
text:
Bring music to life in our school!
Are you passionate about music and inspiring young learners? Do you have the musical knowledge, practical skills and enthusiasm to help children discover the joy of making music together?
We are seeking a registered teacher with strong musical knowledge and know-how to lead music learning across our school from 2027. This is a fixed-term 0.4 FTTE position (two days per week), offering an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference to our ākonga through creativity, collaboration and performance.
You will deliver specialist classroom music programmes for students in Years 2–6 and develop our school music groups and ensembles, creating more opportunities for our young people to explore their creativity, build confidence, perform and feel a strong sense of belonging.
We are looking for someone who can bring music to life through engaging, practical and inclusive learning experiences, nurturing a love of music in every student.
Key responsibilities
Design and deliver engaging, high-quality music programmes for students in Years 2–6, aligned with Te Mātaiaho and the New Zealand Curriculum.
Develop students’ musical understanding and skills through singing, rhythm, listening, composition, movement and practical music-making.
Establish, develop and lead school bands, musical groups and ensembles & support and encourage whole-school singing, helping to build a positive and vibrant musical culture throughout the school.

title: Fixed-term Year 5/6 Classroom Teacher
text:
We seek an enthusiastic, passionate, collaborative, friendly and self-motivated teacher who is able to provide a positive and inclusive learning environment for our ākonga.
The successful candidate must be a highly skilled and reflective practitioner. We are looking for a teacher who has an excellent knowledge of and experience in using the newly refreshed New Zealand Curriculum. Knowledge of BSLA and/or The Code and experience in teaching Structured Literacy and Numeracy would be an advantage. title: Assistant Principal
text:
Kaipara College is seeking an Assistant Principal to join our Senior Leadership Team and lead pastoral care across the school. This is an opportunity for an experienced, relational leader to shape how we support our students and our staff as we strengthen our pastoral systems.
The role
Reporting directly to the Principal, the Assistant Principal will join our senior leadership team with a portfolio assigned to suit their strengths. This may include areas such as pastoral care and leading deans, staff professional learning, curriculum, or other aspects of school leadership. We are interested in what you would bring. This is a teaching role.
Qualities and skills
Proven experience in pastoral care and restorative practice
Experience leading or coaching staff, ideally in a middle or senior leadership role
Sound knowledge of effective, evidence-informed classroom management strategies
Experience working with whānau and external agencies to support students
Confidence using data to identify trends and guide decisions
A commitment to culturally responsive practice and Te Tiriti o Waitangi
A full practising certificate with the Teaching Council of Aotearoa New Zealand
Applicants should state the subject area or areas they teach.
Our school
Kaipara College is a co-educational secondary school serving the Helensville and wider Kaipara community only 35 minutes northwest of the Auckland CBD, situated in Helensville, and recognise the mana whenua of the South Kaipara, Ngāti Whātua o Kaipara.
Our values of Aroha, Whanaungatanga, Kaitiakitanga and Angitūtanga guide everything we do, and we hold high expectations for our students and ourselves.

title: Scale A Classroom Teacher
text:
He aroha ki te ako, kia tuwheratia ai ngā tatau ki te ao.
A love for learning opens many doors.
We are seeking an enthusiastic, caring and collaborative teacher to join our middle school syndicate.
At Woodlands School – Te Akatārere, our tamariki are at the heart of everything we do. We value strong relationships, celebrate identity, language and culture, and encourage everyone to care for themselves, others and the environment.

Creates an inclusive classroom where every learner feels valued and supported.
Uses effective literacy and mathematics teaching practices.
Uses assessment to identify learning needs and plan meaningful next steps.
Demonstrates a commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi, te reo Māori and tikanga Māori.
Contributes to a collaborative team and is open to professional learning.
Implements high-impact teaching approaches to engage learners and support student progress.

title: Physical Education and Health Teacher
text:
Māngere College is seeking a passionate, enthusiastic and committed teacher of Physical Education and Health to join our team in 2027.
We are a vibrant, multicultural secondary school in the heart of Māngere, with a strong sense of community, identity and belonging. We are looking for an innovative and relationship-focused teacher who is committed to making a positive difference in the lives of our young people.
The successful applicant will have sound curriculum knowledge, demonstrate effective and engaging teaching practices, and be committed to raising student achievement. They will be able to build positive relationships with students, whānau and colleagues, and contribute to a collaborative and supportive learning environment.
We value teachers who have high expectations, embrace culturally responsive teaching practices and are committed to providing meaningful learning opportunities that support the wellbeing, confidence and success of all learners.
Leadership opportunities are available within the College in both curriculum and pastoral areas. We welcome applications from experienced leaders as well as teachers who are ready to take the next step in their leadership journey. Applicants interested in these opportunities should outline their relevant leadership experience, strengths and/or leadership aspirations in their cover letter.
A commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi, our school values of Respect and Responsibility, and our motto “Seek the Heights” is essential. Active involvement in the wider life of the school, including sporting and extracurricular activities, is encouraged.
Applicants must hold New Zealand teacher registration and a current practising certificate, or be eligible to obtain these, and have a sound understanding of the New Zealand Curriculum.
Commencement: Term 1 2027.
Please include the vacancy reference # on your application. Applications will be assessed progressively, and interviewing may commence before the advert closes.

title: Full-Time Permanent Year 1–6 Teacher
text:
Are you an enthusiastic, innovative and passionate teacher looking for an opportunity to be part of a supportive and connected school community?

title: Fixed term- Scale A Teacher
institute: Te Manu Tukutuku South Hornby School
text:
Join our passionate team! We’re looking for a skilled, enthusiastic and collaborative teacher who excels at fostering warm relationships with tamariki, whānau, and colleagues.
We prioritise an encouraging approach that notices, values, and celebrates every step of progress our tamariki make – both socially and academically.

title: Principal | Tumuaki U11
text:
Rosehill School is a highly regarded specialist school located in South Auckland, 2 minutes from the Southern Motorway. Employing approximately 260 staff, we cater for ākonga aged 5-21. In addition to our base school, we have 13 satellite sites and a transition unit. We are seeking an experienced, values-led principal with the specialist knowledge, strategic capability and relational strengths to lead our community confidently into its next stage.
This is an exciting opportunity for a highly experienced senior leader with specialist education experience who understands the complexity of supporting learners with diverse and complex needs across multiple sites.
The successful applicant will demonstrate:
deep knowledge of specialist education, individualised learning, neuro-affirming practice and integrated therapeutic support
successful senior leadership of teaching, learning, people and organisational improvement
the ability to establish a clear educational vision and make sound, timely and evidence-informed decisions
strength in developing staff capability, supporting wellbeing and building effective multidisciplinary teams
clear, open and responsive communication, supported by genuine listening and consistent follow-through
commitment to meaningful partnerships with parents, whānau and the wider community
culturally responsive leadership that honours Te Tiriti o Waitangi and strengthens identity, inclusion and belonging
integrity and transparency, including the courage to address complex matters constructively.
Above all, we are looking for a principal who believes deeply in the dignity, capability and potential of every learner. They will be visible, approachable and empathetic, while providing the confident direction and accountability expected of an experienced senior leader.
We welcome visits, please see page 6 of the application pack to arrange a time.

title: Teacher of English
text:
About the position
We are seeking a passionate and suitably qualified teacher to join our well-resourced English faculty. This is a fixed term full-time position covering staff who are on leave or working on specific projects. The suitable applicant will be able to teach up to Year 13. They will have an in-depth knowledge of Level 1 to Level 3 NCEA. Our English faculty is highly supportive of its staff and is collaborative in its approach.
Only teachers with a New Zealand registration, the legal right to work and currently residing in New Zealand should apply.
About our school
Our kura is a co-educational high school in Hamilton, Waikato. We are known for our diverse range of students and our accepting culture. We want all students to succeed and are committed to raising the expectations of students, staff, and whānau to achieve this.
We want all students to work hard in the classroom and to participate in extracurricular activities with passion. We value our staff who get involved in the extracurricular life of the school.

title: Te Reo Māori Teacher
text:
Rangitoto College is seeking a permanent Te Reo Māori teacher to join our Māori (Te Manu Taki) Department to start Term 1 2027.
The successful applicant will deliver engaging, culturally responsive Te Reo Māori education, foster a supportive learning environment, enrich school culture, and willing to teach beyond the Te Reo curriculum.
Please refer to the attached job description for specific details of the role.

Teach Te Reo Māori across various year levels.
Develop and implement culturally relevant and dynamic lesson plans.
Support and encourage students’ language development and cultural understanding.
Collaborate with colleagues to enhance cross-curricular integration of Māori pathways.
Participate in school-wide cultural initiatives and professional development.

A relevant teaching qualification and current registration with the Teaching Council of Aotearoa New Zealand.
Proficiency in Te Reo Māori and a deep understanding of Māori culture.
The ability to teach Te Reo Māori.
Strong communication skills and the ability to engage and inspire students.
A commitment to ongoing professional development and cultural competency.
Why join us?
Be part of a cultural development programme (Tū Rangatira) to enhance cultural identity.
Opportunities for professional growth and development within a supportive Māori department committed to Māori success and excellence.
Contribute to the preservation and promotion of Te Reo Māori and Māori culture.
Be part of our Kaihoe whānau and support our kaupapa: Tū Rangatira, Kapa Haka, Kī ō Rahi and Wānanga Series.
If you are enthusiastic about teaching Te Reo Māori and want to make a meaningful impact on our ākonga and their learning journey, we would love to hear from you.

title: Teacher – Think Big, Teach Boldly, Adventure Beyond the Classroom!

visa.text: Essential: NZ teacher registration, current practising certificate and legal right to work in New Zealand.

text:
Are you the kind of teacher who sees possibilities where others see boundaries?
Mt Somers Springburn School is looking for a passionate, energetic and adventurous person who happens to be a teacher to join our rural school community in 2027.
Nestled beneath the mountains of mid-Canterbury, we believe some of the best learning happens beyond four classroom walls. And with our own school buses, adventure is never far away!
We're looking for passion, not just experience. Whether you're a beginning teacher bursting with ideas or an experienced educator ready to challenge the norm, we want someone who:
Thinks big – challenges conventional approaches and brings fresh ideas.
Makes adventure happen – creates meaningful, real-world learning experiences.
Develops great humans – values wellbeing, relationships, resilience and character alongside academic achievement.
Has high expectations – delivers quality teaching with strong foundations in literacy and mathematics.
Is a doer, not just a dreamer – takes initiative and makes things happen.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and creative teacher to join our team, leading learning in digital technologies and teaching across other learning areas. This is a great opportunity for a beginning teacher who enjoys variety and wants to help ākonga see how digital skills connect to everything they learn.
You will teach digital technologies at Year 7-10, covering computational thinking and designing and developing digital outcomes. Your other teaching areas will be shaped by the needs of our kura and your own strengths and interests, so we'd love to hear what else you can bring.
The terms and conditions, including base salary, for this position is set by the relevant collective agreement.
We are looking for someone who:
holds, or is working towards, a current New Zealand teaching registration and practising certificate
is confident with digital tools and keen to grow their teaching practice
has strengths or interests in other learning areas they would enjoy teaching
builds strong, respectful relationships with ākonga and whānau
is committed to Te Tiriti o Waitangi and culturally responsive practice
works well in a collaborative, supportive team
What we offer
a supportive and welcoming staff and community
ongoing professional learning and development
opportunities to shape digital technologies across the kura
How to apply
Please send a cover letter, your CV and complete the application form attached. In your cover letter, please tell us about any other learning areas you would enjoy teaching.
Safety checking and police vetting will apply to the successful applicant under the Children's Act 2014.

title: Learning Support Coordinator
text:
We are seeking a highly skilled, experienced, and passionate teacher to join our welcoming team as a Learning Support Coordinator (LSC) from Term 1, 2027.
Working closely with our Assistant Principal/SENCo, the successful applicant will coordinate learning support, strengthen inclusive classroom practices and build teacher capability. The SENCo retains management and strategic oversight, while the LSC focuses on coordinating and implementing effective support for ākonga, teachers and whānau.
We are looking for someone who:
Supports learners by understanding their needs and is able to provide timely, culturally responsive support so they can thrive, belong and progress in all aspects of school life.
Support teacher and teacher aide capability to better meet the needs of learners and to strengthen their connections with early learning services.
Encourages and supports parents and whānau to partner successfully with the school and develop an understanding of learning support processes and who to contact if needed.
Has a strong understanding of learning support systems in Aotearoa New Zealand, inclusive education, neurodiversity and diverse learning needs.
Influences others to ensure all learners receive the appropriate support to enhance their learning and progress.
Demonstrates initiative, excellent communication and organisational skills, and a collaborative approach.
Works alongside the SENCo to coordinate specialist services, referrals and learning support resources.
Holds current New Zealand teacher registration and a practising certificate.
For the right candidate, a full-time (1.0 FTTE) position may be negotiated, incorporating additional teaching responsibilities.
About our school
St Joseph's Catholic School is a welcoming, supportive and faith-filled community where relationships, collaboration and the success of every learner are valued. Culturally responsive practice, a commitment to inclusion and a willingness to support the special Catholic character of our school are essential.

title: Year 4 Classroom Teacher
text:
Commencing Term 1, 2027
Are you a passionate, collaborative teacher who wants to make a real difference for learners?
Ngaio School is seeking an enthusiastic and reflective Year 4 teacher to join our learning community for the 2027 school year. We are looking for a teacher who builds positive relationships, creates engaging learning experiences and is committed to helping every child thrive academically, socially and emotionally.
At Ngaio School, we value strong relationships, a sense of belonging, and a learning environment where children are encouraged to be curious, take risks and develop a lifelong love of learning.
We are looking for someone who:
Builds warm, respectful relationships with learners, whānau and colleagues.
Creates an inclusive classroom where every child feels valued, safe and supported.
Delivers engaging, evidence-informed teaching in literacy and mathematics, aligned with the refreshed New Zealand Curriculum.
Uses assessment thoughtfully to respond to learners’ strengths, needs and next steps.
Works collaboratively with colleagues to plan, reflect on practice and improve outcomes for learners.
Communicates effectively with whānau and values the partnership between home and school.
Is committed to culturally responsive practice, honouring Te Tiriti o Waitangi and incorporating te reo Māori and tikanga Māori into everyday classroom life.
What we offer
A welcoming school community that values relationships, collaboration and professional growth.
Opportunities to work alongside colleagues who share ideas and support one another.
A commitment to inclusive practice and equitable outcomes for all learners.
We welcome applications from teachers who bring enthusiasm, sound teaching practice, a growth mindset and a genuine commitment to the wellbeing and achievement of every child.

title: Centre Coordinator

visa.text: NZ residency or a valid NZ work visa

text:
7.5 hours per week | Part-time | Starting 25 January 2027
Tuesday 9.15am – 1.15pm
Wednesday 9.15am – 12.45pm
Permanent position during term time only
About the role
Working in collaboration with centre whānau and other centre support staff, the centre coordinator focuses on building adult capability and confidence.
As the Person Responsible on session, this role provides high-quality support and pedagogical guidance to Playcentre whānau. The Centre Coordinator ensures sessions and programmes reflect Playcentre Philosophy and enriches children’s learning and development.
Duties include, but are not limited to:
Developing whānau to be the first and best educators for their tamariki by ensuring rich, meaningful, child-led curriculum experiences
Role-modelling and supporting the delivery of high quality, whānau-led sessions
Providing advice and support to centre whānau focusing on curriculum, adult education and health and safety to support session delivery
Ensure sessions meet regulatory and legislative requirements including Health and Safety obligations
Recognise the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and how they relate to Playcentre and actively engage in promotion of Māori cultural values
About you
You will be confident building and maintaining strong relationships, providing guidance and solutions with a centre-focused approach.
You will also have:
Passion for Playcentre philosophy and empowering whānau
Course 3 of the Playcentre Education Diploma or equivalent ECE Qualification Level 4+
Confidence using technology to support learning & administration
Strong knowledge of Te Whāriki, ECE regulations, and a commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi
Hold and maintain appropriate First Aid certification
NZ residency or a valid NZ work visa
About us
Formed in 1941, Te Whānau Tupu Ngātahi o Aotearoa – Playcentre Aotearoa is a licensed early childhood education provider and charitable trust. With a philosophy of empowering ‘parents as first educators’, Playcentre seeks to empower whānau and tamariki to work, play, learn and grow together, and today has over 400 centres nationwide.

title: Year 2/3 Teacher
text:
Are you an energetic, passionate educator looking to grow adventurous learners? Paparangi School is seeking two experienced teachers to join our dynamic, collaborative and community-focused team. (As well as a Year 2/3 teacher we also have a vacancy for a Year 4-6 teacher.)
At Paparangi, we’re all about growing adventurous learners. As a proud Enviro-School, we connect our tamariki with the natural world through an authentic, locally responsive curriculum. Our iGROW values underpin everything we do, inspiring our learners to be adventurous learners who get along well with others and are curious about the world around them. Guided by Positive Behaviour for Learning (PB4L), we foster a safe and supportive environment where both staff and student wellbeing is prioritised.
We offer:
A supportive, future-focused team that celebrates collaboration, creativity and mahi tahi.
An extraordinary outdoor learning environment and a vibrant, diverse school community.
Strong, active whānau partnerships that enrich our classroom programmes and extra-curricular activities.
Dedicated leadership committed to our staff’s continuous professional growth and wellbeing.
We are seeking quality teachers who:
Build warm, solid and responsive relationships with tamariki and their whānau.
Thrive in a team-teaching environment and enjoy mahi-tahi with others.
Are reflective practitioners who are committed to ongoing professional development, with a growth mindset and willingness to learn alongside their colleagues
Infuse their classroom with energy, a joy for teaching and a love of learning.
Have experience working with students with additional needs, have an understanding of a range of diverse needs and how to enable them to be the best they can be.
Have strengths beyond the classroom - what can you offer our school? Do you have an interest or skills in digital learning, music, sport or te reo Māori - any of these areas would be an advantage!

title: Teacher of ESOL
text:
Part time option - at least 0.5 FTTE
Epsom Girls Grammar School, Te Kura Tuarua o Ngā Taitamāhine o Maungawhau, is a school that strives for excellence: in performance, in the connections between people and in its pastoral supports. As a school we have always taken girls’ education seriously and, in all that we do, we seek to grow women of great character. In our kura we value courage, aroha, community, and manawa reka, and these values are woven through our words and our actions – from a governance level through to a classroom and co-curricular level, as well as in informal interactions on campus, and in the community.
We are a large, urban school for girls, with a current role of 2,300 students. Our expert staff teach towards the national qualification, NCEA, and we also offer Cambridge International courses and learning (where appropriate). We have a large co-curricular programme of sports, visual and performing arts, cultural expression as well as charity and service opportunities. Our staff are expected to take an active role in supporting the co-curricular programme of the school, by coaching or managing teams and groups.
We are seeking a Teacher of ESOL to join a well developed and supportive department. The successful candidate will be a passionate educator with strong pedagogical skills and an interest in supporting the implementation of the new curriculum. This one year position offers the opportunity to work in a successful department and be part of a friendly, hardworking team.
This position has the possibility of being part time (at least 0.5 FTTE).

title: Future Pathways Advisor
text:
Samuel Marsden Collegiate School is widely regarded as one of Aotearoa’s leading independent schools for girls, from Year 1 to Year 13, with a proud history dating back to 1878. Marsden aspires to lay the foundation for lives of meaning, accomplishment and genuine happiness within our faith-based values-forward environment.
Reporting to the Deputy Principal, the Future Pathways Advisor will guide and support students in Years 10–13 as they explore future study, career and employment opportunities. The role will also support pathways planning across Years 7–13, working collaboratively with staff, families, tertiary institutions, employers and other external providers to ensure students are well informed and equipped to make decisions about their futures.
We are seeking someone who is passionate about helping young people discover their strengths and realise their potential. The successful applicant will have excellent interpersonal and organisational skills, experience in careers education and/or future pathways, and the ability to build strong relationships with a wide range of stakeholders. Proficiency in Google and AI tools is also required.
This is a term-time-only position, Monday to Friday, 8.30am–1.30pm, commencing at the beginning of Term 1, 2027.
This is an exciting opportunity to join a well-established independent school with a strong sense of community, high standards, a clear vision for the future and a hauora-first ethos.
A detailed position description is available on our website www.marsden.school.nz
Applications close Friday 6 November 2026 and will be considered as they are received. Relevant qualifications and experience are required, and safety checking is a condition of employment.
You must have the right to live and work in New Zealand to be considered for this role.

title: Year 4-6 Teacher
text:

Design and deliver personalised, authentic learning programmes tailored to the strengths and needs of ākonga.

text:

Supporting students through observations, data collection and tracking progress
Helping kaiako through building capability

Coordinating services through connecting with external agencies

Working with leadership through resource allocation and creating an inclusive school culture

title: Outdoor Education Teacher
text:
Pukekohe High School is seeking an energetic, innovative, and enthusiastic outdoor education teacher to join our Health and PE faculty in term 1, 2027. Our outdoor education department is well resourced with in-school access to a climbing wall, mountain biking and kayaking.
PHS is a growing school on the southern fringes of Auckland, with a diverse student community. Our vision, Whiria te taangata, whiria te angituu – Weave the people, create success - sets an aspirational goal for our kura. Our values Manaakitanga, Kotahitanga, Aarahitanga and Puumautanga are at the heart of our work. title: Kaiako
text:

We are looking for an enthusiastic full-time kaiako to join our farm-based early childhood centre. Our unique environment provides tamariki with wonderful opportunities to connect with animals, nature and the outdoors, while developing confidence, curiosity, responsibility and a love of learning.

Have strong communication skills

Experienced kaiako are, of course, also very welcome to apply.

title: Learning Support Coordinator
text:

The ability to work with Leadership teams to identify school learning support priorities
Demonstrate an ability to form positive, outcome-based relationships with ākonga/whānau
Demonstrate successful experience in working inclusively and supporting learning needs in the classroom

Position starts Term 1 2027.

title: Occupational Therapist
institute: Blomfield Special School and Resource Ctre
text:

title: Teacher - City School (Mental Health Education Programme)
allowances: Special Duties Allowance, Regional Health Schools Unit
text:
CRHS City is seeking a passionate and adaptable teacher to join our full-day programme supporting students with mental health needs. This rewarding role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of rangatahi who have been out of school due to mental health challenges.
Our integrated programme combines education and therapeutic support, helping students re-engage with learning and work toward successful transitions back to school or alternative pathways. Teachers work in small groups, whole class, and one-on-one, adapting the New Zealand Curriculum to meet individual learning and wellbeing needs.
You’ll collaborate within a multidisciplinary team—including mental health professionals, whānau, and schools of enrolment—to design and deliver personalised programmes that reflect each student’s goals and strengths.
We’re looking for someone who is:
Empathetic, flexible, and trauma-informed in their approach.
Resilient and grounded, with a sense of humour, common sense, and self-confidence.
Demonstrates ethical behaviour, initiative, and a strong commitment to ongoing professional learning - especially in mental health, wellbeing, and inclusive education.
Experienced with strong curriculum knowledge across Years 9-13.
Expertise in senior Mathematics would be an advantage.
Skilled at building trust and leading learning spaces with calm and clarity.
Able to work collaboratively in a multi-disciplinary team environment.
Requirements:
NZ registered teacher with a current practising certificate.
Full, clean NZ driver licence and access to a private vehicle for work travel.
This role involves travel across the greater Wellington region while supporting students with transition. It suits someone who thrives in dynamic environments and values collaboration, resilience, and student-centred practice.
For more details, please contact Jo Fraser, Team Leader [email: see Gazette] , [phone: see Gazette].

Tēna, kōrerohia mo ngā āhuatanga katoa e hiahia ana koe hei tautoko i tō puka tono mo tēnei tūranga.

title: Facilitator – Cambridge and Ngāhinapōuri Communities
text:
Trees for Survival (TfS) is a charitable trust delivering a hands-on environmental restoration and education programme to primary and secondary school students throughout Aotearoa New Zealand.
Our programme takes students, whānau, and local communities on a rewarding journey of growing native seedlings at school and planting them alongside waterways and on erosion-prone land. Through this experience, participants learn about the vital role of riparian planting in climate action, biodiversity restoration, and waterway rehabilitation.
We are currently seeking a passionate Facilitator to support our programme across the Cambridge and Ngāhinapōuri communities of the Waipa District, with the Facilitator responsible for a cluster of five schools.
About the role
This is a part-time contractor position, averaging approximately 30 hours per school each year. As a Facilitator, you will lead, coordinate, and support the successful delivery of the Trees for Survival programme within your allocated schools and communities.
Key responsibilities include:
Building and maintaining relationships with schools, community groups, and landowners.
Coordinating annual potting-on days during September and October.
Conducting plant species counts in November and February.
Organising and facilitating school planting days between May and August.
Undertaking site assessments and monitoring during January and February.
Collecting programme data and preparing reports on planting outcomes.
Supporting schools to engage students in meaningful environmental restoration activities.
About you
We are looking for someone who:
Is proactive, reliable, and enjoys seeing projects through to completion.
Works well independently and as part of a small, passionate, and professional team.
Has strong organisational and relationship-building skills.
Enjoys working with schools, community groups, and volunteers.
Has a sound understanding of, or willingness to learn about, the native flora of Aotearoa New Zealand.
Is enthusiastic about environmental education and restoration.
Apply now
If you are passionate about environmental restoration and education and would like to help inspire young people across the Waipa District, we would love to hear from you.

title: Kaiako Rūmaki Reo
text:
Tēnā koutou e ngā kaiako mā,
E rapu ana mātou i tētahi kaiako e matatau ana ki te reo Māori, e mōhio ana ki te mita o Ngāti Maniapoto, ki ngā tikanga me ngā pūrākau o te rohe, otirā ki ngā kōrero tuku iho o Ōtorohanga.
Ko ngā āhuatanga e hiahiatia ana e mātou i te kaiako hou:
He ngākau nui, he ngākau hihiko ki te mahi kaiako.
He matatau ki te whakaako, ā, e ū ana ki te ako tonu.
He kaha ki te whakawhanaunga me te whakapūmau i ngā hononga pai ki ngā tamariki, ngā whānau, ngā kaimahi me te hapori.
He kura tuatahi whānui tō mātou (Tau 0–8), ā, e rua ngā ara ako: ko te ara auraki me te ara Rūmaki Reo. Hei te tau 2027, ka noho tēnei tūranga ki tō mātou akomanga Teina (Tau 0–3) o te Rūmaki Reo. Tekau mā whitu ngā tauira whakahirahira o taua akomanga, ā, he kaiāwhina wā-katoa hei tautoko i te kaiako me ngā tauira.
Ko ngā uara MANA te tūāpapa o ngā mahi o tō mātou kura. Me whakatinana te kaiako hou i ēnei uara i āna mahi o ia rā, me te raranga hoki i aua uara ki ngā wāhanga katoa o te marautanga.
Mauri ora ki a koutou.
Ngā uara MANA
Manaaki
Manaakitia te tangata, whakanuia tōna mana.
Aroha
Mā te ngākau aroha koe e ārahi.
Nīwha
Ka mahi te tawa uho ki te riri.
Atamai
Whāia te mātauranga, kia koi te hinengaro.
Tēnā, whakaurua ki tō tāhuhu tangata ō tino pūkenga me ō wheako ki ngā mahi ārahi.
Te wātaka whakatū kaiako
I pānuitia: 21 Oketopa 2026
Ka kati ngā tono: 5 Noema 2026, hei te 11 karaka i te ata

title: Kaiako
text:
We are seeking a passionate, dedicated, and enthusiastic Kaiako who has a understanding of, and connection to, Steiner philosophy and its holistic approach to early childhood education. We are looking for someone who is committed to nurturing the whole child, recognising the importance of imagination, creativity, rhythm, nature, and meaningful relationships in supporting children’s learning and development.
The ideal candidate will have a strong work ethic, a positive attitude, and a genuine passion for creating inspiring environments where children feel safe, valued, confident, and empowered to explore the world around them. We are looking for a Kaiako who brings creativity, initiative, and thoughtfulness to their practice, with a particular passion for developing engaging provocations and beautiful, purposeful play spaces that spark curiosity, wonder, imagination, and a love of learning.
Our ideal Kaiako understands the importance of open-ended resources, natural materials, seasonal experiences, and opportunities for children to learn through exploration, imitation, movement, and imaginative play. They will be confident in observing children’s interests and responding with intentional, meaningful experiences that support their individual strengths, developmental needs, and emerging ideas.
We value someone who is reflective, collaborative, and committed to ongoing professional growth. Building respectful, trusting relationships with children, whānau, and colleagues is essential, as is contributing positively to a warm, supportive, and inspiring team environment.
We are looking for a Kaiako who takes pride in their work, demonstrates reliability and dedication, and is willing to go the extra mile to create a nurturing and enriching learning environment. Someone who sees the beauty in everyday moments, values the wonder of childhood, and is passionate about providing children with the time, space, and freedom to develop at their own pace.
If this sounds like you, we would love to hear from you.

Our commitment
To cause learning: We use evidence-informed, structured learning approaches so every learner achieves high-level success.
To make it easy to behave and hard not to: We establish structured, predictable, and culturally safe environments built on high expectations and unconditional care.
To cultivate connection: We know a child’s sense of belonging starts with their teacher.
Who you are

Languages are a highly valued learning area in our school, therefore Glendowie College is committed to maintaining languages as a compulsory subject in the junior school into the future.

We value whakawhanaunatanga and building strong relationships towards our vision to ‘empower ākonga to experience success, ready to embrace their future.’ We have high academic expectations of our students, while also supporting them to develop as confident, articulate, resilient and globally aware young people.

text:

title: Principal/Tumuaki (PRA eligible)
text:

title: Mathematics and Statistics Teacher (Years 9–13)
text:

Assessment: Carry out consistent assessment practices from Year 9-13, maintaining accurate academic and progress tracking on KAMAR.

Schoolwide contribution: Play an active role in driving schoolwide numeracy initiatives and participate fully in the extra-curricular life of the college.
Applicant requirements
Teaching experience: Proven experience teaching mathematics and statistics, with the demonstrated capability to teach across a range of year levels from junior (Years 9–10) through to senior NCEA (Years 11–13).
Curriculum and NCEA knowledge: A strong, comprehensive understanding of the New Zealand Mathematics and Statistics Curriculum and NCEA achievement standards.

title: Kaiako Māori – Te Reo Māori me ngā Tikanga Māori
text:

Our kaupapa is to nurture-inspire-empower, ensuring every ākonga is known, supported and challenged to succeed. As a senior secondary school, we connect academic learning with the real world and support young people to pursue their strengths and aspirations.

Impact projects: Mentor ākonga as they design and lead purposeful projects connected to real needs, interests and community aspirations. Bring your expertise in te ao Māori to support authentic learning, with opportunities in language, Māori arts, heritage and community kaupapa.
Tutorial: Build strong relationships with a group of ākonga, supporting their wellbeing, learning goals and progress. Work alongside whānau and colleagues to ensure each learner has an advocate and no one falls through the cracks.
Working alongside colleagues, whānau and our iwi partner, Te Kawerau ā Maki, you will strengthen opportunities for ākonga to achieve as Māori and enrich cultural understanding across our school.
We welcome a collaborative kaiako who brings strong capability in te reo Māori and tikanga Māori, effective teaching practice, and a commitment to relationships that support rangatahi to thrive. There is scope to shape the role around your strengths and our school’s priorities.
Please state other subjects/supporting subjects/list curriculum areas and teaching experience.

title: KingsGate High School Learning Support Coordinator (SENCO)
text:

Work with students and whānau to understand learners’ strengths, needs, goals and aspirations.
Coordinate the development, review and communication of Individual Education Plans and other learning plans.
Help teachers use effective differentiation, Universal Design for Learning and agreed student-specific strategies. Classroom teachers remain responsible for implementing these strategies.
Work with learning assistants to share learner information and support consistent use of agreed strategies.
Coordinate student-specific collaboration with external specialists and agencies, including RTLB, following established referral processes.
Support the identification of learning needs, assessment, interventions and referrals, and recommend additional resourcing to the Head of Learning Support.
Contribute practical advice and agreed professional learning to strengthen inclusive teaching.
Maintain confidential, timely records; monitor interventions; and report emerging needs or concerns.
Teach an agreed programme based on your subject strengths and the school’s staffing needs.
Contribute to school life and uphold KingsGate’s Christian special character.

Please include a covering letter, CV and referee details. In a letter of no more than 300 words, explain your philosophy of education; what Christian education means to you; how you would live out KingsGate’s Christian special character; your experience supporting diverse learners and coordinating assessment accommodations; and the subjects and year levels you could teach.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced teacher and leader who is passionate about student hauora, engagement and achievement. The successful applicant will lead a faculty committed to developing physical capabilities, promoting healthy lifestyles and supporting students’ personal, social and emotional wellbeing.
We are looking for someone who will:
Provide strong curriculum and pedagogical leadership across health and physical education.
Lead a collaborative faculty focused on student hauora, engagement and achievement.
Support teachers to develop effective, engaging and evidence-informed teaching practice.
Use achievement and assessment information to identify student needs and strengthen learning progress.
Create opportunities for students to develop physical skills, confidence, teamwork, leadership and a lifelong appreciation of physical activity.
Foster an inclusive learning environment that promotes positive relationships, personal growth and wellbeing.
Build strong relationships with students, whānau and colleagues.
Contribute actively to the wider life and leadership of the college.
The successful applicant will be an outstanding classroom practitioner who is student-centred, solution-focused and committed to continuous improvement. They will bring energy, initiative and genuine enthusiasm for health and physical education, alongside the ability to lead, inspire and support colleagues.
At Ōtorohanga College, we value relationships, belonging, achievement and high expectations. Our vision is 'Empowering Learners To Succeed', underpinned by our motto, 'Honour Before Honours'.
We are proud of our students and community and seek a leader who will champion health and physical education, strengthen student hauora and create meaningful learning opportunities that enable every student to thrive.

title: Scale A Release Kaiako
text:
Te Kura o Hinepōhatu (Maidstone Intermediate) is an intermediate kura located in Upper Hutt. We currently have 18 classes split into 5 rōpū across the kura. Guided by our core values of whanaungatanga, manaakitanga, and kaitiakitanga, we foster an inclusive environment where every tamaiti (child) feels a strong sense of belonging. We welcome a diverse range of ākonga who join us from a variety of contributing kura.
We are seeking a dedicated release kaiako to join our kura for 2027 (Year 7 or Year 8 to be decided). The successful applicant will be an enthusiastic kaiako who works collaboratively and maximises opportunities in our innovative learning environment. We seek a kaiako with strong relational skills who brings positive energy to the classroom and actively engages in all aspects of kura life. Our release kaiako will be taking a mixture of CRT release and unit release. At this stage we are looking to cover 1.2 of release throughout 2027.
As an intermediate kura, we value our extracurricular opportunities alongside our academic programmes. Sports, performing arts, clubs, cultural rōpū, ākonga leadership, and many other opportunities abound for our eager learners. Kaiako are encouraged to bring their strengths and passions to support this holistic approach to ākonga development.
We are flexible for the right person and will look at 0.4, 0.6 or 0.8 release options if that appeals more. If you are looking to be a release kaiako for 2027, make contact now.

title: Year 5/6 Team Leader
text:
Are you an inspiring educator and proven leader searching for a school where culture comes first, your professional growth is truly backed and your leadership is valued? This exciting position is opening up for the 2027 school year (starting Term 1)!
Why you’ll love leading here:
A culture that feels like home: We live and breathe relational practice. Step into a genuinely supportive staffroom where you'll build strong, positive relationships with our lead team, staff, tamariki, whānau, and wider community.
Serious investment in you and your team: We don't just talk about growth - our incredible school board actively invests in it! You’ll receive hands-on support in DMIC (Developing Mathematical Inquiry Communities), BSLA (Better Start Literacy Approach), and the Berry Street model (trauma informed practice) while taking an active role in leading staff development, appraisals, and coaching your team.
Room to innovate and drive success: Your voice matters here. As part of our leadership team, you will uphold our school vision and values, model quality teaching, guide curriculum planning, and foster a collaborative environment where team ownership and innovative ideas thrive.
What we are looking for in our team leader:
High-quality leadership in teaching and learning practice, expertise across the curriculum, and a commitment to inclusive education.
Strong interpersonal, self-management, and collaborative skills to support the diverse and changing needs of our learners and team.
A passionate role model who can oversee team assessment, pastoral care, and smooth student transitions while fostering strong whānau and community engagement.

title: Head of Counselling
text:
Start Term 1, 2027 (or earlier by negotiation).
Are you an experienced counselling leader who is passionate about helping young people thrive? We are seeking a Head of Counselling to lead our counselling service and join our collaborative Student Support Services Team. This permanent position is full time (52 weeks). The successful applicant may also be a registered teacher and will report to the Deputy Principal responsible for Student Services. This pivotal role provides the opportunity to shape a coordinated, proactive, and responsive counselling service that supports the wellbeing and success of our diverse students.
As Head of Counselling, you will provide professional leadership for the counselling service and contribute to the strategic direction of student wellbeing across the school.
You will:
hold current membership with the New Zealand Association of Counsellors (NZAC) or an equivalent professional body
provide visible, trusted, and collaborative leadership, building strong professional relationships with students, staff, and the Senior Leadership Team
have experience providing individual counselling to young people, preferably in a secondary school setting
work collaboratively and build positive relationships with students, caregivers, colleagues, school leaders, and the wider pastoral care network
have experience facilitating restorative conversations and processes with young people, caregivers, and staff
have experience assessing support needs, making appropriate referrals, and liaising effectively with external agencies.
